commits.pr_title: [Core][PP] Admit new requests past idle empty steps, and size prefill microbatches from the backlog
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Two scheduling changes for pipeline parallelism with async scheduling, both active only with PP > 1 (admission also requires DP == 1). The original optimization and first implementation are by @gau-nernst (the first two commits). The later commits rework them onto the existing wait-for-output input handling, simplify them, and cut the per-step CPU cost.

- **Admission:** don't let empty steps fill the batch queue and hold back newly arrived requests.
- **PP microbatch cap:** split the outstanding prefill backlog into roughly `pp_size` chunks so a light prefill load fills every stage instead of crossing them one stage at a time.

## Claims

MiniMax-M2.7 (FP8), PP4 × TP1 on one 4×GB200 node, prefill-only traffic (180k-token prompts: 161,984 cached prefix + 18,016 new tokens, 1 output token):

- Mean TTFT at 31% of capacity: **−60%** (5.1 s → 2.06 s); −42 to −47% at 51–66%; −14 to −22% at 82–99%.
- Closed loop: c=1 TTFT halves (3.25 s → 1.62 s); c=2 throughput 0.31 → 0.97 req/s.
- Saturated throughput unchanged (~0.98–1.0 req/s); p90 near capacity about equal.
- No decode regression (2k in / 256 out); decode throughput at c=4/c=16 is 13–18% higher with the cap.
- No behaviour change without PP.

## Validation

### Unit tests

Run on `9ff0cd87561` (this branch's head), CPU only:

```
pytest tests/v1/core/test_async_scheduler.py tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/engine/test_batch_queue_pp_admission.py tests/v1/engine/test_inputs_during_step.py
361 passed, 18 warnings in 68.18s
```

New/changed tests (`-k "pp_microbatch or decode_awaiting or admission or stop_on_add"`: 18 passed in 3.10s, slowest 0.10s):

- `test_batch_queue_pp_admission.py::test_empty_step_admission`: after an unneeded empty step, PP stops scheduling more while it is in flight and waits for a new request; PP=1 and steps a decode needs keep the existing loop. Fails without the last commit (an empty step could otherwise be replaced as soon as the previous one completes, keeping the queue full).
- `test_inputs_during_step.py::test_stop_on_add_returns_at_first_add`: returns at the first added request, including one arriving after the spin period.
- `test_async_scheduler.py`: `test_decode_awaiting_cadence`, `test_pp_microbatch_cap`, `test_pp_microbatch_cap_cached_backlog`, `test_pp_microbatch_cap_skips_decode_only_steps`, `test_pp_microbatch_cap_default_on`, `test_pp_microbatch_cap_progress`.

The fast tests also pass at every commit of the branch.

### End-to-end

Arms: `main` = `94de867077c`; `admit` = this branch with `--pp-microbatch-min-tokens 0` (admission only); `full` = this branch with defaults. Benchmarked on this branch's code before its rebase onto current main (same diff; the rebase only resolved conflicts with #64145). Each arm ran on two nodes (cn13, cn14), in opposite orders; 0 failed requests in every run.

## Details

**Admission** (`EngineCore.step_with_batch_queue`, PP > 1 and DP == 1). With V2 + PP + async scheduling, the engine keeps scheduling steps while the scheduler has requests, even empty ones, because empty steps advance the PP decode cadence (#42187). With prefill-only traffic the empty steps fill the batch queue (`max_concurrent_batches` slots), the engine blocks on the oldest batch, and a request arriving meanwhile waits up to a full PP pass before it is scheduled. This PR:

- keeps at most one empty step in flight that no request needs (`Scheduler.has_decode_awaiting_cadence()` is false). Requests that will decode keep the existing behaviour. Schedulers without the method keep the existing behaviour (interface default `True`).
- with a free batch slot, waits on the oldest batch through the existing input handling in `_wait_for_output` (#65466, #65773), but returns as soon as a request is added so it is scheduled into the free slot. Past the 1 s spin period this keeps checking every 1 ms (sleeping, so the GIL is free) rather than blocking for the rest of the step, which matters when one step takes seconds to cross the stages.
- is off with DP, whose busy loop runs a dummy batch on every step that executes nothing.

**PP microbatch cap** (`Scheduler._pp_microbatch_cap`, PP only; new `--pp-microbatch-min-tokens`, default 4096, 0 disables). The step budget is

`min(max_num_batched_tokens, max(pp_microbatch_min_tokens, num_prefill_lookahead, ceil(uncached prefill backlog / pp_size)) + running decode tokens)`

where the backlog is the remaining prompt tokens of running prefills plus the uncached tokens of waiting requests. A lone 18k-token prompt runs as ~4.5k-token chunks that overlap across the 4 stages; a backlog of `pp_size × max_num_batched_tokens` or more gets the full budget, so throughput under load is unchanged. It is skipped without chunked prefill, with `disable_chunked_mm_input`, or with Mamba-aligned splits, and is never below `num_prefill_lookahead`, so a prefill always progresses.

CPU cost: decode-only steps skip the scan (~0.6 µs at 1,024 running decodes, vs ~150 µs for a full scan); the waiting-queue scan stops once the cap reaches the full budget; only the first `pp_size` waiting requests get a prefix-cache lookup, memoized per request (a 180k-token prompt's lookup is ~4 ms once, then ~2 µs).

**Relation to other PRs.** #68560 (draft) also splits a lone prefill under PP, by applying `long_prefill_token_threshold` to it. This PR sizes chunks from the whole backlog without a user-set threshold, so it keeps splitting when 2–3 prefills are outstanding and returns to the full budget under load, and it adds admission. #68560 reports that admission made 2 × PP2 P/D prefill TTFT p90 worse in their setup; that was a different implementation, but PP2 and P/D are not measured here. #50410 balances decode batches across PP steps and does not overlap.

**Limitations.** Measured on one model and PP size (PP4) with prefill-heavy traffic plus a decode guard; not measured with PP2, multi-node PP (remote readers fall back to blocking), P/D, or mixed prefill/decode traffic. The 1 ms poll after the spin period was not benchmarked in isolation. `--pp-microbatch-min-tokens 4096` may want a larger value on models with a higher fixed per-step cost.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to port, rework, test and benchmark this change.

commits.pr_title: [XPU][LoRA] Support MXFP4 MoE LoRA via XpuFusedMoe hooks
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Support LoRA for the XPU MXFP4 MoE backend (gpt-oss) by applying w13/w2 LoRA deltas through the new `activation_hook` / `output_hook` of `XpuFusedMoe.apply`. Depends on vllm-project/vllm-xpu-kernels#648 (draft until released and `requirements/xpu.txt` is bumped).

## Claims

Builds on #62807 (merged into `main`), which added `LoRAExpertsMixin` and the hook path to `XPUExperts`. This PR enables `XPUExpertsMxFp4` for LoRA (drops its `supports_lora()` opt-out) and runs the existing GPT-OSS LoRA tests in Intel CI — 2 files, ~22 lines.

Not a duplicate: vllm-project/vllm#61310 adds XPU LoRA for FP8/W4A16 by re-implementing the grouped path, and leaves MXFP4 without LoRA. Hooks avoid a second copy of the fused MoE flow; #61310 could reuse this approach instead.

## Validation

AI assistance (GitHub Copilot) was used.

- `tests/lora/test_gptoss_tp.py::test_gpt_oss_lora_tp2` passes on 2x Intel XPU (`enforce_eager=True`; TP>1 + CUDA graph is a separate pre-existing XPU issue, not from this change).
- New `test_xpu_mxfp4_moe_lora_matches_reference` in `tests/lora/test_fused_moe_lora_kernel.py`.

### Accuracy and performance (XPU)

2x Intel Arc Pro B60, `-tp 2`, `--enforce-eager`, LoRA adapter `jeeejeee/gpt-oss-20b-lora-adapter-text2sql`:

```bash
VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn vllm serve openai/gpt-oss-20b \
    --trust-remote-code --gpu-memory-util 0.9 --no-enable-prefix-caching \
    --max-model-len 1024 --block-size 64 -tp 2 --enforce-eager --port 8072 \
    --enable-lora --max-lora-rank 8 \
    --lora-modules sql=$(hf download jeeejeee/gpt-oss-20b-lora-adapter-text2sql)
```

**Accuracy** — GSM8K, 5-shot, 1319 questions, via chat completions (so the request carries the adapter name):

| | accuracy | invalid rate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| LoRA `sql` | 0.7544 | 0.0000 |

A 0 invalid rate and coherent completions rule out the deltas being applied incorrectly (that would produce garbage, not 75% accuracy).

**Performance** — `vllm bench serve`, random 128/128, concurrency 32, 256 prompts, median of 3 runs, 0 failed requests:

| metric | LoRA `sql` |
| --- | --- |
| Output token throughput (tok/s) | 481.05 |
| Request throughput (req/s) | 3.76 |
| Mean TTFT (ms) | 767.38 |
| Mean TPOT (ms) | 60.95 |

MoE LoRA kernels run without a tuned config on this device (`Using default MoE config` for `E=32,N=2880`), so this is a lower bound.

commits.pr_title: [Feature] Add workload snapshots to iteration metrics
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Follow-up to #61690. With `--enable-logging-iteration-details`, stat loggers now also get two workload snapshots, for consumers that model iteration time from the batch composition: the KV context lengths of the requests each iteration ran, and a summary of the waiting queues.

One commit (`a7afc65068`) on `main` (`013ae19bf6`), plus the CI bot's merge of `main`: 14 files, +540/−10, of which `vllm/` is +274/−8 and `scheduler.py` +30/−3.

Changed since the approved revision (`37113e7a3d`): rebased onto current `main`, where the scheduler's `log_stats` argument is now `collect_stats` (#68674), and three of the new tests in `tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py` are removed, as asked in review.

Not a duplicate: #61424 and #61690 (merged) provide the per-iteration counts and the GPU time this builds on; neither reports context lengths or the waiting queues. #53550 (open) adds Prometheus histograms of those counts and reports neither snapshot. Related RFC: #61423.

## Claims

**1. What is added.** Two dataclasses in `vllm/v1/metrics/iteration_workload.py`. All lengths are logical token counts.

| Where | Fields | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `SchedulerIterationDetails.scheduled_workload`, in every iteration record | `sum_prefill_kv_tokens`, `var_prefill_length` | The iteration's prefill requests: sum of their KV context, and population variance of context plus half of the tokens scheduled |
| | `sum_decode_kv_tokens`, `var_decode_kv_tokens` | The iteration's decode requests: sum and population variance of their KV context |
| `SchedulerStats.queued_workload`, in every stats message | `num_prefill_requests`, `sum_prefill_tokens`, `var_prefill_length` | Waiting requests other than those in the next row, counted with all their tokens |
| | `num_decode_requests`, `sum_decode_kv_tokens`, `var_decode_kv_tokens` | Waiting requests that are preempted or wait for remote KV, counted with their computed tokens |

The request and token counts of an iteration are already in its record (#61424). `scheduled_workload` is taken in `schedule()` before the computed tokens advance, and is `None` for dummy iterations. `queued_workload` covers the three waiting queues (`waiting`, `kv_holding_waiting`, `async_kv_waiting`) when the stats are made.

**2. How the queued workload is maintained.** `QueuedWorkloadTally` holds a count, a sum and a sum of squares per category, so reading the summary does not depend on the queue length.

- With the flag, `create_request_queue` wraps each waiting queue in `TalliedRequestQueue`, which reports every request that enters or leaves it. The queue classes and the queue calls in `scheduler.py` are unchanged.
- The tally remembers how it counted each request and subtracts exactly that when the request leaves, because a request's status and computed tokens change while it waits.
- Four places change a waiting request without moving it, and call `Scheduler._refresh_queued_workload(request)`: a streaming session gets its next input, and a remote KV load arrives, fails, or reports invalid blocks. Any new such place has to call it too, or the summary is wrong (see Details).

**3. How the flag controls it.** `--enable-logging-iteration-details` is the only switch.

- Off (default): both fields are `None`, the queues are the plain classes, and no tally exists. `vllm/config/vllm.py`, `arg_utils.py` and `loggers.py` are not touched.
- On: every iteration record carries `scheduled_workload`, and a scheduler built with `collect_stats` keeps the tally and fills `queued_workload`. What is logged does not change (the Iteration lines do not print the workloads), and GPU timing is as in #61690.
- To get the records without the Iteration lines, pass a custom stat logger with `--disable-log-stats` (the third real-engine run below).

## Validation

On commit `a7afc65068` (main `013ae19bf6`), PyTorch 2.14.0+cu130. Two results are from the previous revision (`adc55cd401` on main `878ae13ff0`, same tally code) and are marked.

**The tally equals a scan.** A pytest plugin (not part of the PR) turns the flag on for every scheduler the tests build, and after every `schedule`, `update_from_output`, `add_request`, `finish_requests`, `make_stats` and `reset_prefix_cache` compares the tally with its own scan of the three queues.

| Run | Checks | With waiting requests | Mismatches |
|---|---|---|---|
| Scheduler tests (12 files, 698 tests) | 31,373 | 28,351 | 0 |
| KV and EC connector, streaming, spec-decode and offload tests (40 files, 2,233 tests) | 5,840 | 1,526 | 0 |
| Random driver, 58 configurations × 20 seeds × 150 steps | 1,075,797 | 1,068,058 | 0 |

The driver runs a real `Scheduler` with FCFS and priority queues, sync and async scheduling, async KV loads that arrive, fail or report invalid blocks, `async_kv_waiting`, streaming sessions, aborts and prefix cache resets. On the previous revision, with all four refresh calls disabled, `make_stats()` returned a wrong summary in 15,561 of 52,200 steps, and with any single one disabled in 93 to 9,223. With the flag forced on, 40 tests fail in this environment; 39 of them fail without the flag too, and the other one asserts that there are no iteration details.

**Real engine, one GPU.** `AsyncLLM` with a custom stat logger, `facebook/opt-125m` on one RTX 6000 Ada, `max_num_seqs=4`, 24 concurrent requests with known prompt lengths (20 to 600 tokens) and output lengths (2 to 37 tokens). The check compares what the stat logger received with what those lengths imply.

| Run | GPU timing | Records | Iteration lines | Decode KV tokens, received = implied | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| flag off | – | 0 | 0 | – | pass: no records, `queued_workload` is `None` |
| flag on | yes | 139 | 139 | 128,979 = 128,979 | pass |
| flag on, `--disable-log-stats` | yes | 139 | 0 | 128,979 = 128,979 | pass |
| flag on, `VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING=0` | no | 139 | 139 | 128,979 = 128,979 | pass, `elapsed_ms` is `None` |

In the three runs with the flag, the prefill tokens (6,870) and decode steps (450) also match, every record carries a workload, each of the 144 stats messages carries a queue summary whose request count equals `num_waiting_reqs + num_skipped_waiting_reqs`, and up to 21 requests were waiting.

**Cost per engine step** (previous revision). `schedule()` + `update_from_output()` on one CPU core (i9-10920X) with 256 running requests; the arms alternate on one scheduler, and the numbers are the median time added over the same step without a queue summary.

| Waiting requests | Scan, FCFS | Scan, priority in order | Scan, priority heap unordered | Tally |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 100 | +0.05 ms | +0.10 ms | +0.05 ms | < 0.004 ms |
| 1,000 | +0.27 ms | +1.12 ms | +0.24 ms | < 0.004 ms |
| 10,000 | +2.7 ms | +16.1 ms | +2.2 ms | < 0.004 ms |

The tally column is from the same measurement with 8 running requests, where a step is short enough to resolve it (at most 3.5 µs at 0 to 10,000 waiting); with 256 running it is within the noise of ±0.02 ms. The worst case for the tally is a step in which no request can run and every waiting request is skipped: with 1,000 requests waiting for remote KV, a scan adds 0.13 ms to such a step and the tally 0.86 ms (0.014 ms and 0.087 ms with 100).

**Unit tests.**

```
$ .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py tests/v1/engine/test_iteration_logging.py tests/v1/metrics/test_stats.py tests/v1/metrics/test_logging_stat_logger.py tests/v1/worker/test_iteration_timing.py
3 failed, 367 passed in 187.37s (0:03:07)
$ .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py -k "workload or cached_reservations"
8 passed, 304 deselected in 9.08s
$ .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/metrics/test_engine_logger_apis.py::test_iteration_workload_reaches_custom_stat_loggers
1 passed, 1 warning in 18.76s
```

The three failures need two or three GPUs (`World size (2) is larger than the number of available GPUs (1)`): `test_async_scheduling_pp_allows_rescheduling_with_output_placeholders`, `test_max_loras_counts_running_request_awaiting_output`, `test_diffusion_read_deferral_keeps_a_longer_pp_wait`. The second command selects the new tests and the existing randomized test that now checks the tally; the third starts a real engine. `pre-commit` passes on the changed files.

## Details

- **Why a tally and not a scan.** The previous revision scanned the queues on every step. That is linear in the number of waiting requests, on the engine's scheduling thread, and largest when the engine is overloaded: 0.27 ms per step at 1,000 waiting requests and 2.7 ms at 10,000, and 1.1 ms and 16 ms where a priority queue is read in order, which copies its heap. Reading the heap unordered removes that copy but stays linear. The tally reads in constant time.
- **What the tally costs.** About 0.9 µs per request that enters and leaves a queue. `schedule()` pops and re-queues each waiting request it skips, so a step that skips many pays that for each (the worst case above).
- **Drawback: every in-place change needs a call.** A scan reads the current state; the tally is only right if it is told about every change. The queue wrapper reports the requests that enter and leave, but code that changes the status or token counts of a request that stays in a waiting queue must call `_refresh_queued_workload`. A future change that misses the call raises no error: that request is reported with its old category and length until it next leaves its queue (the error does not accumulate). The streaming-session call has its own test, and the existing randomized async-load test (`test_cached_reservations_admit_like_on_demand_sum`) now asserts on every step that the tally equals a scan, which fails without any one of the other three calls; a new in-place change on a path these tests do not drive would not be caught.
- **Limits.** `queued_workload` is taken when the stats are made, which is later than the iterations in the same message ran, and an idle engine does not update it. A request that was never preempted and whose remote KV has arrived counts as prefill work with all its tokens until it is scheduled. With more than one API server each server's stat loggers get only some of the iterations, as before. With async scheduling and speculative decoding a decode context can exceed the true one by the draft tokens the previous iteration rejects.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][EC] Reuse runner cache hits before remote admission
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Avoid fetching encoder outputs that are already in the consumer's runner cache. Previously, eviction from ECCPU's separate CPU tier could trigger a redundant transfer and fail a metadata-only request if the producer was unavailable.

Related: #55639. No duplicate open PR was found; this fixes consumer admission rather than EPD orchestration or filesystem tiering (#63294).

## Claims

- Reuse valid runner-cache hits during ECCPU admission for both waiting and running requests.
- Keep future hits evictable. If a runner hit is evicted during scheduling, defer the input only when the current chunk needs its embeddings and a remote fetch is still required.

## Validation

Initial CPU validation:

```bash
uv run --no-sync python -m pytest tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py -q -k ec_connector
# 39 passed
uv run --no-sync python -m pytest tests/v1/ec_connector/unit \
  --ignore=tests/v1/ec_connector/unit/test_ec_cpu_connector.py -q
# 417 passed, 28 skipped
```

On `b52bb33d51`, 43 targeted scheduler tests passed. The two-GPU NIXL integration cases were skipped locally because NIXL is unavailable.

Focused regression tests:

```bash
uv run --no-sync python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/ec_connector/unit/test_scheduler_nixl_consumer.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py \
  -q -k 'runner_cache_hit or schedules_evicted_local_runner_hit or placeholder_tokens_without_encoder_embeddings'
```

## Details

ECCPU uses the scheduler's bound runner-cache query to skip remote reads when the embedding count matches. The `ensure_cache_available()` interface keeps its existing two arguments. If a runner hit is evicted during scheduling, the scheduler can load a ready connector copy.

The eviction integration test sizes its consumer cache from the producer's announced entry size.

commits.pr_title: [XPU] Flatten N-D input in XPU W8A16 FP8 linear kernel
commits.pr_body:
`XPUW8A16FP8LinearKernel.apply_weights` overrides `apply_weights` directly instead of `apply_scaled_mm`, so it bypasses the base class's 2D flatten / output-unflatten logic that the other FP8 linear kernels in this file rely on (see `FP8ScaledMMLinearKernel.apply_weights` in `ScaledMMLinearKernel.py`, and `XPUW8A8FP8LinearKernel.apply_scaled_mm` which does `output.view(*output_shape)`).

This mirrors the same class of bug fixed for the XPU MXFP8 linear kernel in #66494 ("Flatten N-D input in XPU MXFP8 linear kernel"). Apply the same fix here: reshape the input to 2D before calling the op and restore the leading dims on the output.

### Root cause (why this only reproduces under torch.compile)

The real oneDNN `fp8_gemm_w8a16` kernel (`vllm-xpu-kernels/csrc/xpu/onednn/onednn_matmul.cpp::check_and_create_output_tensor`) actually supports both 2D and 3D input and *preserves* the leading (batch) dim in its output: 2D in -> 2D out, 3D in -> 3D out. So under plain eager execution, calling this op with a 3D activation happens to work, because the real kernel tolerates it.

However, the `register_fake` meta implementation registered for this op in `vllm/_xpu_ops.py` (`_fp8_gemm_w8a16_fake`) always collapsed its output shape down to 2D `(M, N)`, regardless of input rank:

```python
input_2d = input.view(-1, input.shape[-1])
M = input_2d.size(0)
N = q_weight.size(1)
return torch.empty((M, N), dtype=input.dtype, device=input.device)
```

Under `torch.compile`, Dynamo/AOTAutograd use this fake kernel to infer shapes while tracing, not the real kernel. So a 3D input traces to a 2D fake output, which does not match the 3D tensor the real kernel actually produces at runtime -- this mismatch is what surfaces as a compile-mode-only failure (e.g. for the Transformers modeling backend, which passes 3D activations into vLLM linear layers, see #66494's description).

This PR fixes both sides:
1. `vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear/scaled_mm/xpu.py`: flatten the input to 2D before calling `fp8_gemm_w8a16` and restore the original leading dims on the output, matching the pattern used by the other FP8 linear kernels in this file.
2. `vllm/_xpu_ops.py`: fix `_fp8_gemm_w8a16_fake` to preserve the input rank in its output shape (mirroring the real kernel), so the fake/meta contract is accurate for any caller, independent of whether that caller remembers to flatten first.

After (1), every current caller of `fp8_gemm_w8a16` in this repo already passes 2D input, so (2) is defense in depth rather than strictly required to fix today's bug -- but it keeps the op's compile-time contract correct in general.

### Test plan
No new test added; this follows the exact pattern (`reshape` before / `reshape` after) already used by the other FP8 linear kernels in this file, and by #66494 for the sibling MXFP8 kernel.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Perf][DSv4.1] Use the single-kernel DSv4 top-k on ROCm gfx950
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

On ROCm, DeepSeek-V4/V4.1's sqrtsoftplus routing never reaches vLLM's single-launch Triton top-k (`dsv4_topk`), because `can_use_dsv4_topk()` requires `current_platform.is_cuda()`; it runs the generic HIP `topkGatingSoftplusSqrt` kernel instead. This PR allows `dsv4_topk` on ROCm gfx950 (MI355X, MI350X), and also calls it from the AITER fused-MoE branch of `fused_topk_bias()`, the branch the DSv4.1 ROCm recipe takes (`VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1`). Other ROCm archs keep the HIP kernel. It adds no kernel and is Python only.

**Credit:** this change is Hemanth Acharya's (heachary). He found the gate, measured it and wrote the patch; I ported it onto current main, scoped it to gfx950 and extended the tests. The commit carries a `Co-authored-by` trailer for him.

Related: #64208 (draft) speeds up the same call with a gfx950 Wave64 HIP path; #63180 rewrites the same AITER `sqrtsoftplus` block for fused shared experts; #64277 (draft) computes `sqrt(softplus)` with `log1p` in both kernels; #57478 (closed) fused the gate GEMM with the top-k. See Details.

## Claims

Measured on MI350X. The unit tests, numerics, microbenchmark and GSM8K ran against main `b401405452` (Nov 16), and the serving A/B and GPQA-Diamond against main `952dc48bcf` (Nov 17–18). This PR's code is unchanged from the Nov 16 head except for a review cleanup that moves the `dsv4_topk` check above the AITER branch split and drops a code comment, without changing which kernel runs or its inputs; the head otherwise adds only merges of main.

- **Scope:** on ROCm gfx950, MoE layers that `can_use_dsv4_topk()` accepts now route through `dsv4_topk`, with or without AITER fused MoE: fp32 contiguous logits with 256 or 384 experts, top-6, renormalize, an fp32 correction bias, int32/int64 ids and no hash table. Other ROCm archs (gfx942/MI300, RDNA), hash layers, the 128-expert DSpark draft gate, other scoring functions and CUDA are unchanged. No new env var, config field or kernel.
- **Kernel time:** the top-k drops from 8.6–10.0 to 3.2–3.7 µs at M 1–224, and the router chain (gate GEMM + top-k) by 5.6–7.1 µs. The gate GEMM is untouched.
- **Serving** (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash DP8 + EP8 with MoRI and DSpark K5; random 1Ki and 8Ki tokens in, 1Ki out, C64 to C384; n = 3 fresh-server runs per arm): no config regresses beyond run-to-run noise.
  - **Decode step** (mean inter-token latency): shorter at all eight configs, by 0.48–0.79 ms (0.7–1.7%) at seven of them and by 1.9 ms (2.2%) at 8Ki C256. Four of the eight clear the noise bar. The microbenchmark predicts 0.22–0.33 ms (5.6–8.3 µs per call × 40 MoE layers); the rest isn't profiled, and some of it may be noise.
  - **Output tok/s and TPOT p50** are within noise everywhere except higher throughput at 1Ki C64 (+2.8%). Both follow DSpark's acceptance length, which is sampled and varies by a few percent between runs, so I don't claim a throughput gain. The one throughput cell below main, 1Ki C384 (−0.5%, p 0.36), is inside its ±1.4% bar, and its step is 1.3% shorter.
- **Accuracy:** unchanged. GPQA-Diamond 88.26% → 88.51% (paired by question +0.25 ± 0.57 points, p 0.66), and GSM8K 0.9166 → 0.9242 (inside the combined stderr).
- **Numerics: the same expert ids except at near-ties, weights not bitwise.** Against `ops.topk_hash_softplus_sqrt` (the kernel this replaces), at every M from 1 to 8192 with 384 experts and top-6:
  - **Expert ids** differ only where two experts' selection scores are within 2 fp32 ulp: 35 of 33.6 M rows with N(0, 2²) logits, 24 with N(0, 12²), and 11,625 (0.03%) with logits deliberately clustered at 0.5 + N(0, 1e-3²). Exact ties break the same way (to the lowest expert id), and padding rows give −1 / 0 in both.
  - **Routing weights** differ by at most 1.2e-7 absolute (4.8e-7 relative), from Triton's `tl.log`/`tl.exp` against the HIP kernel's fast-math intrinsics.
  - On CUDA, this same kernel already serves these layers.

## Validation

**Builds:** each has a main arm and a PR arm that adds this PR's files (a clean trial merge), and every container md5-checks the files it copies in.

**Build for the unit tests, id/weight sweep, microbenchmark and GSM8K:** image `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-60bd6dd2edd175a1c55fd3488f871e4c3d2ef27d` (vLLM main `60bd6dd2ed` of Nov 16; torch 2.13.0+rocm10.0.0, triton 3.8.0, AITER 0.1.29), with main `b401405452`'s version of every `vllm/` file changed since the image copied in. The exception is `_custom_ops.py`, whose change needs a rebuilt `_C` and isn't on DeepSeek-V4.1's path.

**Build for the serving A/B and GPQA-Diamond:** image `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-8ca766326652caf4b8e50d1b9118d8a22f6adc73` (vLLM `8ca7663266` of Nov 17; the same torch, triton and AITER, MoRI 1.2.3.post1), with main `952dc48bcf`'s version of all 142 `vllm/` files changed since copied in; the compiled changes in that range are off this path. The PR arm's `vllm/` tree is the PR head `8ff79aec0d`.

- **Unit tests:** the whole `tests/kernels/moe/test_topk_softplus_sqrt.py`, so the HIP-kernel tests are re-checked too; one GPU per run.

  ```
  pytest -v -s tests/kernels/moe/test_topk_softplus_sqrt.py
  VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1 pytest -v -s tests/kernels/moe/test_topk_softplus_sqrt.py
  ```

  | tree | plain | `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1` |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | main | 1676 passed, 7 skipped | 1676 passed, 7 skipped |
  | main + this PR | 1691 passed | 1691 passed |

  - **The 15 extra passes** are the 7 `dsv4` cases that main skips as CUDA-only and the 8 new AITER-path cases. On main's code, this PR's test file fails at collection (it imports `dsv4_topk_platform_supported`). MI355X gives the same counts with the same diff (image `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-083fbac021348c2c7af8a7bc71ba18199d0dd7a4`, main of Nov 9).
  - **Tests:** `test_dsv4_fast_topk` (6 cases) and `test_dsv4_fast_topk_bias_vl` were CUDA-only and now skip unless `dsv4_topk_platform_supported()`. The new `test_dsv4_fast_topk_with_aiter_fused_moe` (gfx950 only, 8 cases) checks with a spy that the AITER branch takes `dsv4_topk`, and compares against the file's torch reference (ids exactly, weights within 2e-5); the comparison with the HIP kernel, which legitimately differs at near-ties, is the sweep below.
  - **CI:** on gfx950 these run in the optional `:amd: (MI355) MoE Kernels` step (`pytest kernels/moe`). They skip on gfx942 (`:amd: (MI300) MoE Kernels`), and CUDA's L4 `MoE Kernels` step runs `test_dsv4_fast_topk` as before. No Buildkite change is needed.
  - **#65972's ROCm-runnable router tests,** plus a check that drives the MoE runner's DP padding branch with a real router, are identical with and without this PR: 71 passed plain; with the AITER env, 70 passed and the same 1 failed in both arms (`test_runner_routes_dp_padding_rows_to_no_expert[True]`, an env assumption in that test).
  - **Lint:** `pre-commit run --files` on the three changed files passes every hook.
- **Ids and weights against the HIP kernel:** both kernels on the same logits at every M from 1 to 8192, with 384 experts, top-6, renormalize and `routed_scaling_factor=1.5`. Every 3rd M has 30% padding rows with NaN logits, every 5th has `bias_vl` rows, and even M use int64 ids, odd M int32. Each distribution covers 33,558,528 rows, 3,353,623 of them padding.

  | logits | identical rows | same experts, other order | other experts | max score gap of a swapped pair (fp64, relative) |
  | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
  | N(0, 2²) | 33,558,384 | 109 | 35 | 1.6e-7 |
  | N(0, 12²), reaching softplus's linear branch | 33,558,415 | 89 | 24 | 1.0e-7 |
  | 0.5 + N(0, 1e-3²), near-ties | 33,516,079 | 30,824 | 11,625 | 2.0e-7 |
  | rounded to 0.5 with a zero bias, exact ties | 33,558,528 | 0 | 0 | - |

  Every set difference swaps two experts whose selection scores, `sqrt(softplus(logit)) + bias` in fp64, are within 2 fp32 ulp; a different order only reorders the top-k slots. Weights, aligned by expert id, differ by at most 1.2e-7 absolute (4.8e-7 relative).
- **Microbenchmark** (one GPU, nothing else running on the node, AITER MoE env as served): the router's `fused_topk_bias(..., "sqrtsoftplus", e_score_correction_bias, 6, renormalize=True)` call, and the router chain, i.e. the gate GEMM (`fp32_router_gemm_dispatch`, GateLinear tier 6) followed by that top-k. One HIP graph per M holds 64 calls with their own inputs (the chain's 128, each with its own gate-weight copy, more than twice the MALL); median of 9 rounds of 20 replays, from CUDA events.

  | M | 1 | 48 | 128 | 224 | 4096 |
  | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
  | top-k, µs main → this PR | 8.61 → 3.18 | 9.90 → 3.52 | 10.04 → 3.52 | 10.02 → 3.69 | 15.72 → 7.93 |
  | router chain, µs main → this PR | 12.01 → 6.46 | 20.15 → 13.24 | 19.90 → 12.86 | 22.41 → 15.35 | 53.21 → 44.92 |
  | router chain, Δ µs | −5.55 | −6.91 | −7.04 | −7.06 | −8.29 |

  Min to max over the 9 rounds is within 0.03 µs at M ≤ 224 (M 4096: 15.69–15.75 µs on main, 7.91–8.27 µs with this PR). torch.profiler shows `topkGatingSoftplusSqrt<6,…>` on main and `_dsv4_topk_kernel` with this PR; the chain's GEMM is the same in both (the low-M Triton kernel at M 1, hipBLASLt from M 48).
- **Serving A/B** (main `952dc48bcf` against this PR, one 8x MI350X node): DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, DP8 + EP8 with MoRI, DSpark K5 and Engram CPU offload. Random data with 1Ki and 8Ki tokens in and 1Ki out (`--ignore-eos`), 4 × C prompts and a fixed seed per config, the same in every boot, with a warm-up before each input length. C64–C256 ran on Nov 17: after one warm-up boot per arm, seven fresh-server boots ran interleaved main, PR, PR, main, main, PR, main, and one main boot was excluded (below), leaving n = 3 per arm. C384, the server's limit (`--max-num-seqs 48` × 8 DP ranks), ran on Nov 18 in six more fresh-server boots interleaved main, PR, PR, main, main, PR, with the same image, trees, server and client. Every client run completed with 0 failed requests and no host memory-pressure stall. `_dsv4_topk_kernel` was compiled only in the PR arm's Triton cache. Every arm, the baseline included, carries an Engram registration patch (`VLLM_ENGRAM_OWN_GPU_REGISTER=1`) for the exit drain that #65595 targets.

  Each cell is main → this PR (Δ, Welch p over 3 + 3 runs); a **bold** Δ is larger than twice the larger same-arm sd. Mean ITL is the decode step, since the client receives one streamed chunk per engine step.

  | ISL | C | output tok/s, main → this PR | TPOT p50 ms | mean ITL ms (decode step) | acceptance length |
  | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
  | 1Ki | 64 | 4,592 → 4,720 (**+2.8%**, p 0.03) | 11.98 → 11.68 (−2.5%, p 0.32) | 30.28 → 29.78 (**−1.7%**, p < 0.01) | 2.513 → 2.519 (+0.2%, p 0.90) |

  - **How to read it:** TPOT p50 and output tok/s move with DSpark's acceptance length. That is sampled: the client sends no temperature, so requests run at the server default (1.0, unseeded), and a run's acceptance length varies by a few percent. Across these eight configs the PR doesn't shift it: paired by prompt, the precision-weighted difference is −0.16% ± 0.27% (± stderr). So throughput and TPOT p50 mix the step change with acceptance noise, and mean ITL isolates the step.
  - **An earlier n = 2 run** (1Ki only, on main `b401405452`) read output tok/s −0.4% at C128 and +1.3% at C256, and TPOT p50 +0.3% at C256. Here they are +0.7% (p 0.70), +1.3% (p 0.24) and −0.9% (p 0.42). All are inside noise in both runs, so the C128 dip was not a regression.

```
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 --language-model-only \
  --data-parallel-size 8 --enable-expert-parallel --all2all-backend mori_high_throughput \
  --moe-backend aiter --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 \
  --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":true,"embedding_across_dp":true}' \
  --attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype":"mxfp4","indexer_sparse_logits":true}' --block-size 128 \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","rejection_sample_method":"block","enable_adaptive_verification":false}' \
  --max-num-seqs 48 --max-num-batched-tokens 4096
vllm bench serve --backend vllm --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --tokenizer <checkpoint> --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 \
  --dataset-name random --random-input-len {1024,8192} --random-output-len 1024 --ignore-eos --seed <one per config> \
  --max-concurrency {64,128,256,384} --num-prompts <4 x C> \
  --percentile-metrics ttft,tpot,itl,e2el --metric-percentiles 50,90,99,99.9,100 --save-result --save-detailed
# warm-up before each input length: 1024 in at C64 (128 prompts, 1024 out); 8192 at C32 (64 prompts, 256 out)
```

</details>

- **Accuracy:**
  - **GPQA-Diamond** (serving build, on a second MI350X node; #65992's setup: simple-evals prompt and answer regex through the chat API, thinking on at `reasoning_effort` high, temperature 0.6, top_p 0.95, max_tokens 65,536, seed 1000 × repeat + question index, 256 requests in flight): 8 repeats of the 198 questions per arm, over six interleaved fresh-server boots. Main 88.26 ± 1.42%, this PR 88.51 ± 2.00% (mean ± sd over repeats). Paired by question, the difference is +0.25 ± 0.57 points (± stderr, p 0.66); the design detects about 1.6 points. 54 of each arm's 1,584 responses hit max_tokens; without them, 91.37% → 91.63%.
  - **GSM8K** (first build; lm-eval 0.4.12 `local-completions`, 5-shot, `temperature=0`, all 1,319 questions, `num_concurrent=256`), once per arm on the same server configuration: main 0.9166 ± 0.0076, this PR 0.9242 ± 0.0073 (strict-match; flexible-extract 0.9174 → 0.9234). The difference, +0.0076, is inside the combined stderr (0.0105).
- **Not covered:** gfx942 (MI300X) and RDNA, which keep the HIP kernel; widening the gate needs an MI300X run of the unit tests and the microbenchmark. On MI355X only the unit tests ran on this branch.

## Details

**Why `dsv4_topk` can run on gfx950, and only there for now.**
- **PDL:** the kernel is plain Triton apart from the PDL intrinsics (`gdc_wait`, `gdc_launch_dependents`). Those sit behind the `launch_pdl` constexpr, `current_platform.is_arch_support_pdl()`, which is False on ROCm, so they compile out.
- **Launch shape:** one program (one warp) per row is the right shape on CDNA too. Hemanth swept 1–16 rows per program × 1–4 warps on MI355X, and the shipped config was the fastest: 3.42 µs, against 14.97 µs at 16 rows per program.
- **gfx950 only:** the kernel assumes nothing about the wave size (masked loads, and `tl.max`/`tl.min`/`tl.sum` reductions with `num_warps=1`), but its numerics and speed on gfx942 and wave32 GPUs are untested. #64208 gates its fast path to gfx950 the same way.
- **Why it's faster:** the generic kernel's time is nearly flat in M, a fixed cost per call; #64208 traces it to 32 B per lane of scratch and the per-round argmax reductions.

**Changes** (+37/−27 in two source files, +70/−5 in the test file):
- **`router/dsv4_topk.py`:** a new `dsv4_topk_platform_supported()` (`is_cuda()`, or `is_rocm()` and `on_gfx950()`) replaces `current_platform.is_cuda()` in `can_use_dsv4_topk()`. It also guards the kernel definition, so the kernel is only defined where it can compile and launch.
- **`router/fused_topk_bias_router.py`:** `fused_topk_bias()` checks for `dsv4_topk` once, before it splits into the AITER fused-MoE and non-AITER branches, instead of only inside the non-AITER branch as on main. The check is main's, with `get_moe_padding_mask()` passed inline, so padded rows still get id −1 and weight 0. The AITER blocks it now precedes (`biased_grouped_topk` and #67107's `topk_gating`) handle sigmoid and softmax only, so nothing else moves.
- **`masks_padding`** (from #65972) is unchanged and stays False under AITER fused MoE. For `sqrtsoftplus` it was already conservative on main, and its only reader (the MoE runner's DP path for TRT-LLM FP8 monolithic kernels, CUDA SM100 only) isn't reached on ROCm.

**Fused shared experts, and #63180.** On main, `FusedTopKBiasRouter._compute_routing()` appends the fused shared-expert slots with `torch.cat` after `fused_topk_bias()` returns, so the append applies to `dsv4_topk`'s output as to the HIP kernel's. #63180 instead passes `(M, top_k + n)` out-buffers so the HIP kernel writes the shared columns itself in the AITER `sqrtsoftplus` block; the `dsv4_topk` check returns before that block. If both land as written, results stay correct (#63180's width check falls back to the `cat` append), but its zero-kernel append is lost on these layers. So whichever PR merges second skips the fast path when out-buffers are passed: one check on the `dsv4_topk` condition, which keeps #63180's in-kernel append for its prefill band and this fast path for decode batches. The two conflict in context only.

**Overlapping work.** No open or merged PR enables `dsv4_topk` on ROCm or calls it from the AITER branch (searched Nov 4 and Nov 9 over PRs updated since Oct 1; re-checked Nov 16).
- **#64208** (draft) targets the same call differently. The µs figures come from different benchmarks and builds, so they are not a controlled comparison:

  | | #64208 | this PR |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | approach | a gfx950 Wave64 HIP path inside `topkGatingSoftplusSqrtKernelLauncher` (C++, needs a rebuild) | enables vLLM's existing Triton `dsv4_topk` on ROCm gfx950 (Python only) |
  | time per call, graph replay, 384 experts | 5.38–5.80 µs at 1–256 rows on MI355X (its description) | 3.2–3.7 µs at 1–224 rows on MI350X; 3.27–3.43 µs at 32–256 rows on MI355X (Hemanth's microbenchmark, an older build) |
  | weights and ids vs the generic kernel | bit-identical | weights within 1.2e-7; ids the same except at near-ties |
  | coverage | 256/384/512 experts, hash and non-hash rows; gfx950 only | 256/384 experts, non-hash rows; gfx950 only |

  They compose: if both land, this path takes the non-hash 256/384-expert layers, and #64208 serves hash layers and 512 experts. The author of #64208 has no concerns with this PR proceeding.
- **#64277** (draft): if it lands first, I'll re-measure and restate the numerics above.
- **#57478** (closed, "not significant e2e perf improvement") fused the gate GEMM with the top-k; this PR leaves the gate GEMM untouched.
- **Co-application** (`git merge-tree` on main `b401405452`): this PR adds a test-file-only conflict with #64277 and #63687, and none with the other open PRs that touch these files.

**Limitations:** not bitwise with the HIP kernel (weights within 1.2e-7, ids at near-ties; GSM8K and GPQA-Diamond unchanged). Hash layers, the 128-expert DSpark draft gate (top-3) and other expert counts keep the HIP kernel (#64208 covers hash rows and 512 experts), and on ROCm only gfx950 takes the fast path.

**AI assistance:** AI tools (Claude, in Cursor) helped port Hemanth's patch onto current main, write the added test, resolve the merge with main, search for overlapping work and draft this description. I have reviewed every changed line, and ran the GPU tests, benchmarks and evals above myself on MI350X and MI355X, with AI assistance. The PR commit and the Nov 12 merge of main carry a `Co-authored-by: Claude` trailer.

commits.pr_title: [Perf][Kernel][GDN] Fuse the prefill causal conv1d + post-conv prep into one CUDA kernel
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Fuse the GDN prefill causal conv1d and post-conv prep (`causal_conv1d_fn` + `fused_post_conv_prep`) into one CUDA kernel for pure-prefill batches (Qwen3-Next, Qwen3.5, Qwen4Exp). The conv output no longer round-trips through HBM: **3.0–3.2× faster at 16–32K tokens** (5.0–5.3 TB/s), 1.2–2.2× at smaller sizes. End to end, prefill throughput is **2.0% higher** on Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8 (TP1, GB300). AI assistance (Kimi Code, Claude Code) was used.

## Claims

- From 4K tokens the fused kernel moves the op's minimum traffic at 3.5–5.3 TB/s (80% of a 6.6 TB/s device copy at 32K); the stock chain stays at ~1.65 TB/s.
- Conv state is **bitwise-identical** to the stock chain; q/k/v are within ~2 bf16 ULP (fp32 conv products, `tanh.approx` SiLU), `g`/`beta` follow the stock formulas.
- **No H / HV specialization.** Head counts are runtime arguments; the only template parameter is the chunk size (16 / 32 / 64), so 3 variants cover any head count, GQA ratio and TP split.
- **Packed FP32 (`f32x2`) is sm_103a-only.** With nvcc 13.1 and 13.4, the FFMA2 / FMUL2 path spills in sm_100a / sm_100f cubins and runs 20% slower, so those images use scalar FMAs. CMake adds an sm_103a image for this file next to the regular arch list, so B300 / GB300 always get `f32x2`. B200 (sm_100) runs the scalar path and is not benchmarked here.
- Supports `beta_scale` (`linear_allow_neg_eigval`, OLMo Hybrid), so those models also take the fused path.
- Other batches (any decode rows, conv bias, non-SiLU, head dim ≠ 128, ROCm) keep the stock chain.
- GSM8K unchanged.

## Validation

```bash
pytest tests/kernels/mamba/test_gdn_fused_mtp.py
# 28 passed (GB300, 35d1a666c5); kernel vs stock chain and `_forward_core` fused vs stock, incl. beta_scale=2.0
```

Other GDN tests (`test_fused_gdn_post_conv.py`, FlashInfer / CuTeDSL prefill, `forward_core_split`, output projection, `ba_overlap`): 211 passed.

**Kernel** (GB300, H=16, HV=48, K=V=128, MTP3 conv state, bf16; CUPTI, CUDA graph, cold L2; median of 3 interleaved rounds, alternating order, rounds within 1% above 64 tokens). TB/s is the op's minimum HBM traffic (read x/a/b and conv state, write q/k/v/g/beta and conv state) over time, same bytes for both arms.

| Tokens | Stock chain | This PR | Speedup |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 64 | 9.9 µs (0.30 TB/s) | 8.2 µs (0.37 TB/s) | 1.21× |
| 256 | 12.5 µs (0.88 TB/s) | 9.6 µs (1.14 TB/s) | 1.29× |
| 1024 | 31.1 µs (1.38 TB/s) | 16.4 µs (2.61 TB/s) | 1.89× |
| 4096 | 108.2 µs (1.58 TB/s) | 49.0 µs (3.48 TB/s) | 2.21× |
| **16384** | 412.3 µs (1.65 TB/s) | 135.8 µs (5.01 TB/s) | **3.04×** |
| **32768** | 823.0 µs (1.65 TB/s) | 257.2 µs (5.29 TB/s) | **3.20×** |
| 16 × 1024 | 412.5 µs (1.66 TB/s) | 137.8 µs (4.97 TB/s) | 2.99× |

One sequence per row except the last. Without a CUDA graph (GDN prefill runs outside piecewise graphs), the stock chain's two launches add host gaps: 96.6 vs 8.0 µs at 64 tokens.

**E2E** (Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8, TP1 on one GB300, prefix caching off, 16K-token chunks; Rust frontend and Rust bench). main is `e04f069197`, the merge base; this PR is `7d9b7ef1be` (the later commit only trims comments). Mean of 2 runs per arm (order main / PR / PR / main, fresh server each); runs within 0.1% for prefill and 1.5% for TPOT.

| Workload | Metric | main | this PR | Change |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 16K in, 1 out, c16 | Input throughput | 48.9k tok/s | 49.9k tok/s | **+2.0%** |
| 32K in, 1 out, c8 | Input throughput | 48.4k tok/s | 49.3k tok/s | **+2.0%** |
| 4K in, 512 out, c32 | Mean TPOT | 16.23 ms | 16.22 ms | −0.1% |

With 1 output token every step is pure prefill, so the fused path runs in all 36 GDN layers: 6.6 ms saved per 16K-token step (335 → 328 ms), two thirds of the kernel-time estimate (36 × 276 µs = 9.9 ms). The 4K/512 run has decode rows in most steps, so it keeps the stock chain.

**Accuracy** (same servers, temperature 0, thinking off):

| Task | main | this PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| GSM8K 5-shot (n=2638, flexible-extract) | 96.89% | 96.93% |

<details>
<summary>Commands</summary>

```bash
VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1 vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8 --port 8123 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 --max-num-seqs 32 \
  --max-model-len 40960 --language-model-only --reasoning-parser qwen3

# (IN, N, C) = (16384, 64, 16), (32768, 32, 8); 2 warmups at 32K. Mixed: 4096 in, 512 out, N=128, C=32
VLLM_USE_RUST_BENCH=1 vllm bench serve --backend vllm --base-url http://localhost:8123 \
  --model Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8 --dataset-name random \
  --random-input-len $IN --random-output-len 1 --prompt-token-ids --ignore-eos --seed 0 \
  --num-prompts $N --max-concurrency $C --num-warmups 4
```

</details>

## Details

- **Kernel** (`csrc/mamba/gdn_prefill_conv.cu`): each warp streams a chunk of one sequence's tokens over one head's channels, L2-normalizes q/k, writes v, and computes `g`/`beta` for V heads. A device-side radix-32 search over `query_start_loc` replaces the host chunk table.
- **Dispatch**: `gdn_prefill_conv_supported` gates on a pure-prefill batch, bias-free width-4 SiLU conv, bf16, head dim 128 and 8-byte row alignment; a `hasattr(torch.ops._C, ...)` check falls back on older builds.
- **Build**: the sm_103a gencode is added when `nvcc >= 12.9`. CUDA-only: the inline PTX `tanh.approx` does not hipify.
- Related: #66946 tunes the ROCm prefill conv kernels; separate platform and code path.

<details>
<summary>bench_gdn_prefill_conv.py</summary>

```python
"""Fused GDN prefill conv (gdn_prefill_conv) vs stock causal_conv1d_fn +
fused_post_conv_prep. Device time via CUPTI, cold L2; median of 3 interleaved
rounds with alternating arm order. GB/s = the op's minimum HBM traffic (same
byte count for both arms) / time."""

import statistics

import pandas as pd
import torch
from flashinfer.testing.utils import bench_gpu_time_with_cupti

from vllm.model_executor.layers.mamba.ops.causal_conv1d import causal_conv1d_fn
from vllm.model_executor.layers.mamba.ops.gdn_prefill_conv import gdn_prefill_conv
from vllm.third_party.flash_linear_attention.ops.fused_gdn_prefill_post_conv import (
    fused_post_conv_prep,
)
from vllm.v1.attention.backends.utils import compute_causal_conv1d_metadata

H, HV, D, WIDTH = 16, 48, 128, 4  # Qwen3.5-style GDN, TP1
DIM = (2 * H + HV) * D
STATE_LEN = WIDTH - 1 + 3  # MTP3 conv state
ROUNDS = 3
# (num_seqs, tokens per seq)
CASES = [(1, 64), (1, 256), (1, 1024), (1, 4096), (1, 16384), (1, 32768), (16, 1024)]


class Meta:  # prebuilt causal_conv1d metadata, as the layer passes it
    def __init__(self, qsl_cpu, device):
        self.nums_dict, self.batch_ptr, self.token_chunk_offset_ptr = (
            compute_causal_conv1d_metadata(qsl_cpu, device=device)
        )


def min_bytes(T, num_seqs):
    x_in = T * DIM * 2
    qkv_out = T * DIM * 2
    ab_in = 2 * T * HV * 2
    gbeta_out = 2 * T * HV * 4
    state = 2 * num_seqs * DIM * STATE_LEN * 2  # read + write
    return x_in + qkv_out + ab_in + gbeta_out + state + DIM * WIDTH * 2


torch.manual_seed(0)
dev = torch.device("cuda")
rows = []
for num_seqs, L in CASES:
    T = num_seqs * L
    x = torch.randn(T, DIM, device=dev, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
    ba = torch.randn(T, 2 * HV, device=dev, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
    b, a = ba[:, :HV], ba[:, HV:]
    w = 0.5 * torch.randn(DIM, WIDTH, device=dev, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
    A_log = torch.randn(HV, device=dev)
    dt_bias = torch.randn(HV, device=dev)
    state0 = torch.randn(num_seqs + 1, DIM, STATE_LEN, device=dev).to(torch.bfloat16)
    qsl_cpu = torch.arange(0, T + 1, L, dtype=torch.int32)
    qsl = qsl_cpu.to(dev)
    cache_idx = torch.arange(1, num_seqs + 1, dtype=torch.int32, device=dev)
    has_init = torch.ones(num_seqs, dtype=torch.bool, device=dev)
    meta = Meta(qsl_cpu, dev)
    s_stock, s_fused = state0.clone(), state0.clone()

    def stock():
        y = causal_conv1d_fn(
            x.T, w, None, conv_states=s_stock, query_start_loc=qsl,
            cache_indices=cache_idx, has_initial_state=has_init,
            activation="silu", metadata=meta,
        ).T
        return fused_post_conv_prep(y, a, b, A_log, dt_bias, H, D, D)

    def fused():
        return gdn_prefill_conv(
            x, w, s_fused, qsl, cache_idx, has_init, a, b, A_log, dt_bias, H, D
        )

    # Correctness first (one call each from the same state).
    ref, out = stock(), fused()
    for name, got, want in zip("qkvgb", out, ref):
        diff = (got.float() - want.float()).abs().max().item()
        tol = {"q": 0.0125, "k": 0.0125, "v": 0.064}.get(name, 1e-4)
        assert diff <= tol, (num_seqs, L, name, diff)
    torch.testing.assert_close(s_fused, s_stock, atol=0, rtol=0)

    times = {"stock": [], "fused": []}
    for r in range(ROUNDS):
        order = ["stock", "fused"] if r % 2 == 0 else ["fused", "stock"]
        for arm in order:
            fn = stock if arm == "stock" else fused
            t = bench_gpu_time_with_cupti(fn, cold_l2_cache=True, use_cuda_graph=True)
            times[arm].append(statistics.median(t) * 1e3)  # ms -> us
    nbytes = min_bytes(T, num_seqs)
    st, fu = (statistics.median(times[k]) for k in ("stock", "fused"))
    rows.append(dict(
        seqs=num_seqs, tokens=T, stock_us=st, fused_us=fu, speedup=st / fu,
        stock_GBps=nbytes / st / 1e3, fused_GBps=nbytes / fu / 1e3,
        stock_rounds=[round(v, 1) for v in times["stock"]],
        fused_rounds=[round(v, 1) for v in times["fused"]],
    ))
    print(rows[-1], flush=True)

print(torch.cuda.get_device_name(), torch.__version__)
print(pd.DataFrame(rows).to_string(index=False, float_format=lambda v: f"{v:.2f}"))

# Achievable-bandwidth reference: a 1 GiB device copy (read + write).
src = torch.empty(1 << 29, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=dev)
dst = torch.empty_like(src)
t = statistics.median(bench_gpu_time_with_cupti(lambda: dst.copy_(src), cold_l2_cache=True))
print(f"copy: {2 * src.nbytes / (t * 1e-3) / 1e9:.0f} GB/s")
```

</details>

commits.pr_title: [Perf][Multimodal] Reuse OpenCV capture for video metadata
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Reuse the already-open OpenCV capture when reading video metadata. Since #61759, `decode_opencv()` opens a capture for frame reads and `get_video_metadata(data)` opens another decoder for the same bytes, adding CPU work before the first token.

```diff
 decode_opencv(data)
   cap = open_video_capture(data)
-  get_video_metadata(data)          # opens another capture
+  get_video_metadata(data, cap=cap)
   read_frames(cap, ...)
```

## Claims

- Remove the redundant decoder open for ordinary MP4 and missing-frame-count inputs. Keep the demux-only frame-count fallback and MP4 edit-list correction.
- Preserve single-frame video decoding by skipping its unnecessary end-of-stream metadata probe.
- Preserve standalone `get_video_metadata(data)` calls through an optional keyword-only capture argument.
- Cover real MP4, live WebM and raw H.264 decoding with the default and Qwen2-VL samplers; verify identical decoded frames/metadata and one decoder open.

## Validation

### November 23 review follow-up

The review's one-frame MP4 reproducer fails on `fedb1a5a` with both `frame_recovery=False` and `True` and returns shape `(0, 64, 64, 3)` instead of one frame. The shared capture is left at EOF by the metadata end-seek. The correction now probes only when the reported frame count exceeds one, preserving the only frame and retaining the existing multi-frame edit-list correction.

In a fresh, independent uv environment (Python 3.12.13, vLLM 0.33 precompiled extensions, Torch 2.14.0 and OpenCV 5.1.0), with CUDA invisible:

```bash
# Before the guard, 2 failed with zero frames.
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES='' uv run --no-sync python -m pytest tests/multimodal/test_video.py \
  -k single_frame_video_survives_metadata_probe -o addopts='' -q

# After the guard, 17 passed.
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES='' uv run --no-sync python -m pytest tests/multimodal/test_video.py \
  -k 'single_frame_video_survives_metadata_probe or reuses_capture_for_metadata or edit_list_trimmed or demux_counts or recovery or unknown_source_fps' \
  -o addopts='' -q --disable-warnings
```

These checks exercise real OpenCV captures through `VideoBackend.load_bytes`, including the two one-frame read paths and the original format, sampling, trim and recovery cases. The serving benchmarks below were performed on November 9. Model serving and performance were not rerun for this review fix. Codex assisted with the reproduction, fix, regression tests and this update.

### Original November 9 validation

**Regression:** With the new test on the unmodified decoder, all six cases fail with `assert 2 == 1`. With this patch, the targeted suite passes: **15 passed**, including edit-list trimming, missing frame counts, unknown FPS and frame recovery.

```bash
# Before: 6 failed, each at assert decoder_opens == 1 (actual: 2).
uv run --no-sync python -m pytest tests/multimodal/test_video.py \
  -k reuses_capture_for_metadata -o addopts='' -q

# After: 15 passed.
uv run --no-sync python -m pytest tests/multimodal/test_video.py \
  -k 'reuses_capture_for_metadata or edit_list_trimmed or demux_counts or recovery or unknown_source_fps' \
  -o addopts='' -q
```

The new tests are selected by the existing CPU multimodal Buildkite step (`pytest -v -s -m 'cpu_test' multimodal`). Local tests run current-main Python sources with the compatible vLLM 0.33 precompiled extensions and Torch 2.14.0; this patch changes no kernels.

**Controlled end-to-end diagnosis:** Qwen/Qwen3-Omni-30B-A3B-Instruct, two H200 GPUs (reported as L20X on this host), vLLM 0.33.0 / Torch 2.14.0+cu130, vLLM-Omni `4b63581c`, async chunk, FA3/Triton MoE, fixed vLLM 0.32 client and seed 0. After an initial corpus pass, the same server alternated stock → capture reuse → capture reuse → stock using a process-local probe. Each run had 40 requests at 0.5 requests/s and 100 output tokens; 27/40 inputs contain video. This isolates the mechanism implemented by this patch.

| Mode | Runs × requests | Mean TTFT (run range), ms | Mean E2E, ms | TPOT, ms/token |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Stock | 2 × 40 | 200.83 (199.98–201.68) | 645.55 | 4.4879 |
| Reuse | 2 × 40 | 173.84 (173.29–174.38) | 620.32 | 4.5055 |

TTFT decreases by **26.99 ms (13.44%)**. Both reuse runs produce the same 40 texts and token lengths as the stock reference. A same-process stock/reuse/reuse/stock CPU decode check saves 41.23 ms per two-frame MP4, with identical frame hashes; 27/40 video requests predict approximately 27.83 ms aggregate TTFT savings.

**Submitted patch validation:** Applied the exact changed `opencv.py` (matching file hashes) to an isolated vLLM 0.33 runtime, without the diagnostic monkeypatch. Both 40-request runs pass (80/80, zero failures); the warm run measures 174.47 ms TTFT and 622.79 ms E2E. 40/40 warm generated texts and all per-request token lengths match the stock reference. This additional run used another reserved H200 pair on the same host and is reported separately from the controlled A/B above.

**Static checks:** All applicable hooks pass with `pre-commit run --files vllm/multimodal/video_decoders/opencv.py tests/multimodal/test_video.py`, including Ruff, mypy and CI test tethering.

Use the [Qwen3-Omni deployment configuration at the tested Omni revision](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/blob/4b63581cf6527dc5c964558650e996c0a36e027a/vllm_omni/deploy/qwen3_omni_moe.yaml), with model snapshot `26291f793822fb6be9555850f06dfe95f2d7e695`:

## Details

The metadata path already resets the capture after its edit-list seek; the existing trimmed-MP4 and frame-recovery tests exercise the reused capture. Missing-frame-count inputs still use their separate demux-only pass. The regression test tracks real OpenCV captures, excluding that necessary demux pass, without timing thresholds.

Duplicate-work checks found no open PR removing this redundant open. Related #62505 addresses stream lifetime/release and #60612 isolates OpenCV decoding; neither removes this second decoder. This reversible change is limited to the shared OpenCV decoder and its tests, with no new user configuration.

The local H200 results support the TTFT step seen when Omni upgraded to vLLM 0.33. They are not H100 absolute-latency measurements and do not explain the separate November 8 TPOT increase.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Exclude frontend and install-time env vars from compile factors
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Excludes the Rust frontend switches and the precompiled-install switches from `envs.compile_factors()`, so switching between the Python and Rust frontends, or running from another checkout, no longer invalidates the torch.compile cache.

## Claims

- `VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND`, `VLLM_USE_RUST_BENCH`, `VLLM_RUST_FRONTEND_PATH`, `VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED`, `VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED_RUST`, and `VLLM_SKIP_PRECOMPILED_VERSION_SUFFIX` no longer feed the compile cache key.
- Compiled graphs are unaffected. The Rust frontend's only engine-side effect, forcing `mm_device_do_normalize` off, is still hashed through `MultiModalConfig.compile_factors()`.

## Validation

On head `58ca4d2f56` (base `d6d1616c1c`).

Env hash (`hash_factors(envs.compile_factors())[:12]`):

| Environment | main | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| default | `db12ea6534a4` | `fb8a5b242e32` |
| `VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1 VLLM_RUST_FRONTEND_PATH=/a/vllm-rs` | `a3017f2681bd` | `fb8a5b242e32` |
| `VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1 VLLM_RUST_FRONTEND_PATH=/b/vllm-rs` | `5e7fc0ae4eb6` | `fb8a5b242e32` |

```
$ pytest tests/test_envs.py -k compile_factor --durations=0
5 passed, 55 deselected, 2 warnings in 1.21s
```

The new `test_frontend_and_install_envs_are_not_compile_factors` fails on main (`AssertionError: assert False`). `tests/test_envs.py`: 60 passed. `tests/config/test_config_utils.py -k compile_factors`: 3 passed.

## Details

**Root cause.** `compile_factors()` hashes every known vLLM env var that is not in `ignored_factors`. Engine processes inherit the frontend's environment, so `VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1` changes the key although the engine compiles the same graphs. `VLLM_RUST_FRONTEND_PATH` is worse: its getter resolves to the absolute path of the packaged `vllm-rs`, so every checkout or worktree gets its own key. The precompiled switches only matter at install time, like `VLLM_SKIP_VERSION_SUFFIX`, which is already ignored.

**Engine-side effect.** `ModelConfig._resolve_mm_device_do_normalize()` reads `VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND` and forces `mm_device_do_normalize` off. The resolved value is a `MultiModalConfig` field that is not in that config's `ignored_factors`, so it stays in the config hash. One model's profiling processor also reads the flag, but only to raise an error without it.

**Tradeoff.** Dropping entries from the env factors changes the default hash once (`db12ea6534a4` to `fb8a5b242e32` above), so existing compile caches miss once after upgrading, as with any change to `ignored_factors`.

---

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Gate opt-in features at startup through typed flags
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Some opt-in features that the Rust frontend does not implement are accepted at startup and then served as 501 routes: `/tokenizer_info` under `--enable-tokenizer-info-endpoint` and the Cohere v2 chat routes under `VLLM_ENABLE_COHERE_API` (placeholders from vllm-project/vllm#62432 and vllm-project/vllm#65376). A gap that is decidable at startup becomes a request-time failure. The gates are also split: some are CLI flags in the typed config, while `routes.rs` reads others from the environment, and `UnsupportedArgs::check` reads `VLLM_MAX_TOKENIZE_TOKENS` (vllm-project/vllm#67348) from the environment, which only the `--args-json` path calls, so `vllm-rs serve` ignores the variable.

This PR makes every feature switch a flag in the typed config. Where Python exposes a switch only as an environment variable, Rust binds a hidden flag to that variable and parses it as Python does, as `--server-dev-mode` already does for `VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE`. A switch for a feature Rust does not implement fails startup like any other `Unsupported` argument. On the Python-supervised `--args-json` path, Python resolves these variables through `vllm.envs` and passes the values in the JSON, so the Rust frontend reads no environment there.

## Claims

| Python switch | Rust flag | Python parsing | Rust behavior |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--enable-tokenizer-info-endpoint` | same, now `Unsupported` | flag | startup refusal; the 501 `/tokenizer_info` route and its config field are removed |
| `VLLM_ENABLE_COHERE_API` | hidden `--enable-cohere-api` (`Unsupported`) | `bool(int(value))` | startup refusal when on; the 501 `/cohere/v2/chat` and `/cohere/v2/chat/render` routes are removed |
| `VLLM_ENABLE_RESPONSES_API_STORE` | hidden `--enable-responses-api-store` (`Unsupported`) | `bool(int(value))` | startup refusal when on; today Rust ignores the variable and silently serves the stateless Responses API |
| `VLLM_MAX_TOKENIZE_TOKENS` | `--max-tokenize-tokens` (`Unsupported`), now bound to the variable with `env = ...` | `int(value)`, unset when blank; the flag takes precedence | startup refusal on both paths; `vllm-rs serve` used to ignore the variable |
| `VLLM_ALLOW_RUNTIME_LORA_UPDATING` | hidden `--allow-runtime-lora-updating` | `value.strip().lower() in ("1", "true")` | unchanged behavior; the value now reaches the router through `ApiServerOptions` instead of `std::env::var` in `routes.rs` |

- Flag names follow the existing hidden env flags: the variable name without the `VLLM_` prefix (`VLLM_SKIP_MODEL_NAME_VALIDATION` → `--skip-model-name-validation`).
- Each switch takes effect on both launch paths. Under `vllm-rs serve`, clap reads the variable through `env = ...`. Under `vllm serve`, the Python supervisor passes the value `vllm.envs` resolves in `--args-json`, as it already does for `VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S` and `VLLM_HTTP_TIMEOUT_KEEP_ALIVE`. `_RUST_FRONTEND_ENV_ARGS` in `vllm/v1/utils.py` maps each argument to its variable; a set variable is passed unless the CLI flag already put the argument in the JSON, which keeps Python's precedence for `--api-key` and `--max-tokenize-tokens`. This also covers the other hidden env flags (`VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE`, `VLLM_MAX_N_SEQUENCES`, ...) and `VLLM_API_KEY`, which `apply_env_fallbacks` used to read by hand on the Rust side; it is removed, and the hidden fields are now deserialized from the JSON.
- Python leaves out a value that keeps the setting off (`False`, `None`, or an empty string), as it leaves out defaults, so `VLLM_ENABLE_COHERE_API=0`, `VLLM_ENABLE_RESPONSES_API_STORE=0`, and a blank `VLLM_MAX_TOKENIZE_TOKENS` start under `vllm serve`. Under `vllm-rs serve`, the unsupported switches refuse every set value, including `0`, like any `Unsupported` argument.
- An invalid value now fails in `vllm.envs`, as with the Python frontend (`VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE=true` raises `ValueError: invalid literal for int() with base 10: 'true'`). JSON has no infinity, so `VLLM_LOG_STATS_INTERVAL=inf` is passed as the largest float, which Rust reads as "never log", as before.
- The list of unsupported arguments names the variable bound to an argument, whose value may come from the environment (`- enable_cohere_api (VLLM_ENABLE_COHERE_API)`), and then says to unset it.
- The `Unsupported` refusal message drops its suggestion to pass the argument to the Python engine after `--` and reads "Remove this argument, or unset the environment variable bound to it, to continue." Arguments Rust does not define are already forwarded to the engine, an argument marked `Unsupported` is frontend-owned, and an environment variable cannot go after `--`.
- The second commit makes `--args-json` errors report the error itself. A function value parser made clap print `invalid value '<the whole JSON>' for '--args-json <JSON>': ...`, and the JSON holds every non-default argument Python forwards, which buried the error. A small `TypedValueParser` now reports the error as is (`error: The following arguments are not implemented in Rust frontend yet: ...`).
- The third commit, for vllm-project/vllm#67348, binds `VLLM_MAX_TOKENIZE_TOKENS` to `--max-tokenize-tokens` and drops the environment read from `UnsupportedArgs::check`.
- The fourth commit moves the environment reading on the `--args-json` path from Rust to Python, as described above.
- The Rust CI lane starts the `test_tokenization.py` server without `--enable-tokenizer-info-endpoint`; it already deselects the `tokenizer_info` tests.

## Validation

Rebased onto `9bb2b593b9` (head `788ddb68ec`; the only conflict was a comment line in `.buildkite/test_areas/rust_frontend.yaml`): fmt, sort, deny, clippy and nextest pass on each commit (2914, 2914, 2914, 2912 tests).

On `366664fcda` (base `443b51e52f`):

```
cargo fmt --all -- --check                                                        # ok
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings     # ok
cargo nextest run --workspace --all-features --locked --no-fail-fast
# Summary [15.274s] 2899 tests run: 2899 passed, 13 skipped
pytest tests/entrypoints/launchers/api_server/test_api_server_process_manager.py -k rust_frontend
# 17 passed, 8 deselected
```

Tests:

- `test_rust_frontend_receives_resolved_env_settings` (new, Python): with no variable set, nothing is passed; on values reach `--args-json` as `vllm.envs` resolves them (`inf` as the largest float, `0` for the request body size, `VLLM_API_KEY` as a string); off values (`0`, blank, empty) are left out; `--api-key` and `--max-tokenize-tokens` win over their variables. Dropping the off-value filter fails it.
- `unsupported_env_switches_fail_startup` (new): for the three unsupported switches, `0`, `1`, and `true` are refused under `vllm-rs serve`, and the argument in `--args-json` is refused with its variable named; the messages are snapshotted.
- `args_json_reads_env_only_settings` (was `args_json_reads_env_only_settings_from_env`): the eight hidden settings are read from the JSON, with defaults when absent, `0` removing the body size limit, and the largest float meaning "never log".
- `log_error_stack_defaults_to_server_dev_mode` and `enable_scale_out_defaults_to_server_dev_mode`: the `--args-json` half takes `server_dev_mode` from the JSON.
- `unsupported_args_fail_startup`: adds `--enable-tokenizer-info-endpoint` on both paths.
- `serve_args_forward_env_only_settings_to_frontend_config`: adds `VLLM_ALLOW_RUNTIME_LORA_UPDATING` (on, off, and a non-truthy value).
- `lora_routes_follow_api_server_options` (new, next to `dev_routes_follow_api_server_options`): the LoRA routes follow `ApiServerOptions`.
- Removed: `cohere_routes_follow_the_python_gates` and `tokenizer_info_route_follows_api_server_options`, which asserted the 501 placeholders.

`--args-json` built by the Python supervisor for each environment, then parsed by the `vllm-rs` debug binary (`vllm-rs frontend` with unused fds, so a start that passes argument parsing stops at the engine connection):

```
# VLLM_ENABLE_COHERE_API=1 VLLM_MAX_TOKENIZE_TOKENS=4096
{"enable_cohere_api": true, "engine_ready_timeout_secs": 600, "http_timeout_keep_alive": 5, "max_tokenize_tokens": 4096, "model_tag": "Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B"}
error: The following arguments are not implemented in Rust frontend yet:
- enable_cohere_api (VLLM_ENABLE_COHERE_API)
- max_tokenize_tokens (VLLM_MAX_TOKENIZE_TOKENS)

Remove these arguments, or unset the environment variables bound to them, to continue.
# VLLM_ENABLE_COHERE_API=0 VLLM_ENABLE_RESPONSES_API_STORE=0 VLLM_MAX_TOKENIZE_TOKENS=
{"engine_ready_timeout_secs": 600, "http_timeout_keep_alive": 5, "model_tag": "Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B"}
invalid engine-core client configuration: inherited ZMQ listener fd 999999 is not open
# VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE=1 VLLM_LOG_STATS_INTERVAL=inf VLLM_API_KEY="a b" VLLM_HTTP_MAX_REQUEST_BODY_SIZE=0 VLLM_MAX_N_SEQUENCES=8
{"api_key": "a b", "engine_ready_timeout_secs": 600, "http_max_request_body_size": 0, "http_timeout_keep_alive": 5, "log_stats_interval": 1.7976931348623157e+308, "max_n_sequences": 8, "model_tag": "Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B", "server_dev_mode": true}
invalid engine-core client configuration: inherited ZMQ listener fd 999999 is not open
```

`vllm-rs serve`, release binary from `a7d4d474ae` (the fourth commit does not change this path):

```
$ VLLM_ENABLE_COHERE_API=1 vllm-rs serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B
error: invalid value '1' for '--enable-cohere-api <ENABLE_COHERE_API>': argument is not implemented in Rust frontend yet

Remove this argument, or unset the environment variable bound to it, to continue.
$ VLLM_MAX_TOKENIZE_TOKENS=4096 vllm-rs serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B
error: invalid value '4096' for '--max-tokenize-tokens <MAX_TOKENIZE_TOKENS>': argument is not implemented in Rust frontend yet
$ vllm-rs serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --enable-tokenizer-info-endpoint
error: invalid value 'true' for '--enable-tokenizer-info-endpoint [<ENABLE_TOKENIZER_INFO_ENDPOINT>]': argument is not implemented in Rust frontend yet
```

GPU validation (GB200, one node, `vllm-rs` built from `a7d4d474ae`, before the fourth commit; `HuggingFaceTB/SmolLM2-135M-Instruct` for the probes):

```
# VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1, test_tokenization.py with the CI filter (server starts without --enable-tokenizer-info-endpoint)
5 passed, 4 deselected in 75.95s
# VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=0, test_tokenization.py, full file (server keeps --enable-tokenizer-info-endpoint)
9 passed in 55.18s
# VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1, test_lora_adapters.py with the CI filter (VLLM_ALLOW_RUNTIME_LORA_UPDATING through --args-json)
10 passed, 3 deselected in 58.48s
```

`vllm serve` with `VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1` exits 1 for each probe (the same command with no switch becomes healthy), with the Rust frontend's error right before Python's `RuntimeError: Frontend process failed during engine core initialization. See root cause above.`:

```
# --enable-tokenizer-info-endpoint
error: The following arguments are not implemented in Rust frontend yet:
- enable_tokenizer_info_endpoint

Remove these arguments to continue.
# --max-tokenize-tokens 4096
error: The following arguments are not implemented in Rust frontend yet:
- max_tokenize_tokens
```

## Details

- **Why a hidden flag.** One mechanism for every gate: the typed config carries each switch, the startup check sees all of them, and nothing below the CLI layer reads a gate from the environment. Value-typed environment settings, such as media limits, are a different case and stay out of this PR.
- **Where the refusal lives.** The env-only unsupported switches are `Option<Unsupported>` fields in `ServerUnsupportedArgs`, next to `--enable-tokenizer-info-endpoint`, grouped by what they configure rather than by where Python reads them. Under `vllm serve` they reach `UnsupportedArgs::check` through the JSON like any other unsupported argument, so a refusal reads the same whether a flag or a variable set it.
- **Why Python resolves the variables.** An earlier revision had the Rust frontend read them on the `--args-json` path too: a clap overlay that rebuilt the command without defaults, `required`, or clap's own environment reading, and wrote the matches over the deserialized arguments with `update_from_arg_matches`. Passing the values from Python makes `--args-json` self-contained, reuses Python's own parsing, leaves out off values without a Rust parser per variable, and removes the dependence on how clap-derive updates fields. The cost is that a new Rust argument bound to a variable also needs a row in `_RUST_FRONTEND_ENV_ARGS`.
- **`vllm-rs serve` and off values.** That path has no Python in front to resolve the variables, and accepting `0` there would need a value parser per variable that mirrors Python's. `vllm-rs serve` is a separate entry point, so no existing deployment moves to it with the defaults spelled out.
- **Python tests.** The forced-Rust lane starts no other server with these switches on: `tests/entrypoints/openai/responses/conftest.py` already leaves the store variable unset under Rust, the Responses tests that set it (`test_harmony.py`, `test_parsable_context.py`, `test_mcp_tools.py`) and `tests/entrypoints/multimodal/openai/responses/test_image.py` are not in the Rust lane, nor are the Cohere tests. `test_lora_adapters.py` sets `VLLM_ALLOW_RUNTIME_LORA_UPDATING`, which keeps working.
- **Related.** vllm-project/vllm#46081 (draft, last updated 2026-06-29) implements `/tokenizer_info` in Rust; if it lands, the `Unsupported` marker gives way to the flag. No other open PR covers these gates.
- **Behavior change.** A Rust frontend deployment with `--enable-tokenizer-info-endpoint`, `VLLM_ENABLE_COHERE_API=1`, or `VLLM_ENABLE_RESPONSES_API_STORE=1` now fails at startup instead of serving 501s or silently dropping the store. Under `vllm-rs serve`, `VLLM_MAX_TOKENIZE_TOKENS` now fails startup instead of being ignored, and so does any set value of the three unsupported switches, including `0`. Under `vllm serve`, an invalid value of a variable the Rust frontend reads now fails in `vllm.envs` with Python's error instead of a Rust one.

commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Read the Docs warns that the HTML build is 1474 MB ([main build](https://app.readthedocs.org/projects/vllm/builds/36139787/) on ba4b266dfa), over its 1024 MB per-format limit ("Builds over this limit may fail in the future"). This brings it to 466 MB.

## Claims

- `show_source: false` removes the inline "Source code in ..." listings, which were ~80% of large API pages (e.g. `vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler` went from 1.82 MB to 198 KB).
- Excluding `vllm.models` from `api-autonav` drops 1139 generated pages. The `autoref_code` hook now skips `vllm/models` too, so inline code naming those classes no longer links to missing pages.
- A post-page hook strips the indentation Material's recursive nav templates add to the header and sidebar (~118 KB per page). Page content, including code blocks, is untouched.

## Validation

Full local `mkdocs build`, each step applied cumulatively on top of ba4b266dfa. The final build has no warnings, and the rendered text of every page is identical with and without the nav hook once whitespace is collapsed.

| Step | Site size | HTML files |
|---|---|---|
| main | 1457 MB | 3962 |
| + `show_source: false` | 1084 MB | 3962 |
| + exclude `vllm.models` | 785 MB | 2823 |
| + strip nav indentation | 466 MB | 2823 |

```bash
mkdocs build -d site && du -sm site && find site -name '*.html' | wc -l
```

## Details

#58705 removed the `minify` plugin to speed up the build. Re-enabling it on top of this PR gives 443 MB but adds ~55 s locally, so the hook gets 93% of its saving at a fraction of the cost and needs no extra dependency.

commits.pr_body:
## Overview
In prefill, all ranks did the same norm, router and shared-expert work on all tokens, and the all-reduce sent bf16 data. Now each rank does this work on a quarter of the tokens and sends FP4 data. Steps spend less time in communication.

## Claims
Speed up prefill by reducing comms time in the all gather phase of the all reduce operation.

## Validation
MoE half of a layer vs stock: 
1024 tokens −9%; 
2343 −20%; 
14394 −33%.

Fused combine + reduce-scatter on top: 
2343 189.6→170.3 µs; 
5857 469.8→366.0; 
14394 1145→853.

Eval | With our changes | Baseline (stock main)
-- | -- | --
GSM8K (flexible / strict) | 0.846 / 0.831 | 0.844 / 0.826
GPQA-Diamond | 84.09% | 82.68%

## Details
Prefill TP4 all reduce comms are bandwidth bound. Currently, we (typically) do a two shot all reduce with RS in bf16 and AG in bf16, preceded by rmsnorm and residual add, and followed by router, topk/sort and quant.

This changes the order so we do reduce scatter first. Then on the quarter of the rows held in each GPU we do the rmsnorm and residual add, followed by the router, shared experts and the sorting for MoE and quantizing the activations to fp4. This is followed by an all gather in fp4 of the activations, and the metadata.

The shared expert activations remain on the owner ranks. they are added after the subsequent reduce scatter before moving to the next attention layer. This allows us to keep the shared expert output local and not paying the price of all gathering that.

Requires AITER #7771.
