commits.pr_title: [Kernel] ReplaySSM: cache SSM inputs for faster Gated DeltaNet standard decode
commits.pr_body:
Supersedes [#48792](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48792), closed when the source fork was deleted.

## Background

This is the second sub-PR split from the large draft PR [#47576](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/47576), which presents the full ReplaySSM design across Mamba2 and Gated DeltaNet for both standard and speculative decode. The first sub-PR, Mamba2 standard decode ([#48018](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48018)), landed as `866fea2b9`, so this is a plain diff against main. It lands the next stage: Gated DeltaNet (GDN) standard decode. ReplaySSM caches recent SSM inputs instead of writing the recurrent state back to HBM on every step. It is a collaboration between Dao AI Lab and NVIDIA, and the full derivation and figures are in the [blog post](https://dao-lab.ai/blog/2026/replayssm/). AI assistance was used for parts of this work, and the authors have reviewed every changed line.

## Core concept

GDN decode is memory-bound. Each step loads and stores the delta-rule recurrent state (a `head_v x head_k` matrix per value head), and that per-step state store dominates HBM traffic. ReplaySSM keeps a small ring buffer of recent per-step inputs (the key `k`, the corrected value `d`, and the scalar gate `g`) together with a periodic checkpoint state. On most steps it reconstructs the state and reads the output from the checkpoint plus the buffer, and it writes the full state back only on periodic flushes, once every `L` steps, where `L` is the buffer length. On the non-flush steps the per-step state store becomes a small input append, which removes the dominant traffic.

The baseline only becomes bandwidth-bound at large batch. The table below reports the DRAM bandwidth the baseline `fused_recurrent_gated_delta_rule_packed_decode` reaches, as a percentage of peak, measured in isolation with cold L2 at `L=16`.

| bs | H100 fp32 | H100 fp16 | B300 fp32 | B300 fp16 |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 9.0% | 5.9% | 6.5% | 3.9% |
| 8 | 35.2% | 27.5% | 24.2% | 18.0% |
| 32 | 71.3% | 54.8% | 56.7% | 39.1% |
| 128 | 84.5% | 79.6% | 78.3% | 68.6% |
| 256 | 86.3% | 83.4% | 82.4% | 74.5% |
| 512 | 87.5% | 85.3% | 84.5% | 77.4% |

At small batch the per-request state footprint is tiny and the launch grid is small, so too few memory transactions are in flight to cover HBM latency, and the kernel is latency-bound rather than bandwidth-bound. In a hybrid model the small-batch step is also dominated by the MLP layers, not the SSM layers. Small batch is therefore not the target regime. ReplaySSM targets serving batch, where the GDN kernel saturates HBM and the per-step state store is the bottleneck.

## What this PR adds

Everything here is opt-in. With the feature off, the decode path is byte-for-byte the baseline.

- The GDN cached decode kernel `fused_recurrent_gated_delta_rule_replayssm` (state-reconstruction route), plus its hardware-keyed launch-config helper (`_gdn_decode` in `replayssm_config.py`).
- No new config flags. It reuses the two flags added in #48018: `--use-replayssm` turns on cached decode, and `--replayssm-buffer-len` sets the history buffer length `L` (default 16).
- Integration. The Qwen3.5 GDN mixer dispatches to the kernel under the flag, the GDN attention metadata builder carries the per-row ring cursor, and the state-shape and state-dtype calculators size the extra `d`/`k`/`g` caches on the paged state. Single-token prefill rows route to the prefill path rather than the cached decode kernel. The conv path reuses vLLM's `causal_conv1d_update` unchanged.
- Prefix caching. Align mode (`--mamba-cache-mode align`) is supported: the builder re-anchors the ring at each mamba block start and forces a flush on the block-completing step, so the checkpoint carries the exact block-boundary state for reuse and cached prefixes match the baseline.

This covers standard (non-speculative) decode only.

## Design notes

### Paged cache layout

The input ring caches (`d`, `k`, `g`) and the checkpoint state live inside the paged KV block, appended as extra tensors on the baseline `(conv, ssm)` state, for five tensors total. They stay live across decode steps, the checkpoint until the next flush and the ring across many steps, so they must sit in HBM between kernel launches. Appending them onto the paged state reuses vLLM's per-request block allocation and block-table indexing directly. `g_cache` is fp32; the `d` and `k` caches use fp16 when activations are bf16 for better numerical precision.

### CUDA graphs and continuous batching

Whether a row flushes is per-row runtime data. Under continuous batching the rows in one captured batch sit at different buffer positions, so the flush status varies across the batch and cannot be a compile-time constant, even for standard decode. The write position is `decode_step mod L`, computed on the host each step from scheduler token counts and copied to the device asynchronously, so no device-to-host sync is needed. The metadata builder computes the per-row flush flag on the host (a row flushes at its last buffer slot, `write_pos == replayssm_buffer_len - 1`, and, in align prefix-caching mode, on the step that completes a mamba block) and passes it to the kernel as a per-row input, so one captured graph per batch size covers both the non-flush and the flush rows. Deriving the cursor from `decode_step mod L` each step also means recycled paged blocks need no zero-init.

## Results

Unlike the Mamba2 sub-PR, GDN has no tuned/default baseline split. The shipped launch config is the swept per-hardware optimum, and the baseline is vLLM's `fused_recurrent_gated_delta_rule_packed_decode` at its own config, so every speedup below is a single honest number.

Two models are evaluated: Qwen3.5-4B (BF16) on one H100 and Qwen3.5-122B-A10B-NVFP4 on one B300, at buffer length 16 with fp32 and fp16 SSM state, greedy, and CUDA graphs on. End-to-end numbers are produced with `benchmarks/replayssm/e2e_decode_speedup.py`.

> **Blackwell (B300) support:** this sub-PR ships a Triton kernel only, and on B300 that Triton kernel is bandwidth-capped for fp16 state (44% DRAM utilization). fp16 state on B300 is therefore not enabled in this sub-PR. fp32 state is not capped this way and reaches 1.49x at bs512, but is still suboptimal.
> A CuTe-DSL kernel targeting Blackwell removes the cap, and is planned as a subsequent separate PR. At bs512 it lifts the B300 kernel-level speedup from 1.49x to 1.66x for fp32 state, and from 1.05x to 1.61x for fp16 state.

### End-to-end speedup

Whole-model per-step speedup, `standard ms/step / ReplaySSM ms/step`, greedy, CUDA graphs on.

| bs | Qwen3.5-4B H100 fp32 | Qwen3.5-4B H100 fp16 | Qwen3.5-122B B300 fp32 |
|---:|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0.99x | 0.99x | 0.96x |
| 8 | 1.03x | 1.01x | 1.03x |
| 32 | 1.08x | 1.03x | 1.09x |
| 64 | 1.14x | 1.05x | 1.11x |
| 128 | 1.21x | 1.06x | 1.16x |
| 256 | 1.27x | 1.07x | 1.20x |
| 512 | 1.30x | 1.08x | 1.22x |

ReplaySSM wins most at serving batch, where the GDN layers take a growing share of the step, and stays roughly break-even at bs 1 to 8. fp16-state end-to-end on the dense 4B is lower than fp32-state because the fp16 GDN kernel is a smaller share of the MLP-dominated step.

### Kernel-level speedup

Isolated per-kernel CUDA-time speedup.

| bs | H100 fp32 | H100 fp16 | B300 fp32 | B300 fp16 |
|---:|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0.88x | 0.58x | 0.51x | 0.39x |
| 8 | 1.34x | 1.07x | 1.16x | 0.85x |
| 32 | 1.54x | 1.27x | 1.37x | 0.94x |
| 128 | 1.66x | 1.37x | 1.44x | 1.04x |
| 256 | 1.68x | 1.39x | 1.46x | 1.05x |
| 512 | 1.67x | 1.41x | 1.49x | 1.05x |

Kernel speedup rises with batch and saturates by about bs 128 to 256. fp16 state on blackwell is not supported in this sub-PR.

### Buffer length

Isolated per-kernel speedup vs the baseline. Each cell lists buffer length `L` = 8 / 16 / 32, with the best of the three in bold.

| model | bs 8 | bs 32 | bs 256 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3.5-4B (H100) fp32 | 1.27x / **1.33x** / 1.21x | 1.46x / **1.54x** / 1.43x | 1.58x / **1.68x** / 1.59x |
| Qwen3.5-4B (H100) fp16 | 1.04x / **1.05x** / 0.94x | 1.24x / **1.27x** / 1.10x | 1.34x / **1.39x** / 1.20x |
| Qwen3.5-122B (B300) fp32 | 1.13x / **1.17x** / 1.11x | 1.28x / **1.37x** / 1.31x | 1.36x / **1.46x** / 1.40x |

Speedup is bell-shaped in buffer length, trading flush frequency against per-step traffic. `L=16` is best in every entry and is the shipped default.

## Tests

Correctness is checked at four levels, all on GDN.

Per-step kernel correctness lives in `tests/kernels/test_replayssm_standard_decode_gdn.py`. Every decode step is checked against the baseline packed-decode kernel over multi-flush sequences, across six state and activation precision combinations, the production model geometries (small, Qwen3.5-4B, Qwen3.5-122B), buffer lengths 4 and 16, strided and contiguous layouts, and continuous batching with per-row buffer positions and null-padded slots. A separate case sweeps per-row write positions across a batch. Tolerances are near-exact at fp32 (output rtol 1e-4, atol 1e-4; state rtol 1e-3, atol 2e-3), tight enough to catch a TF32 matmul-precision regression, and looser at bf16 and fp16 where rounding dominates.

Prefill and decode equivalence lives in `tests/kernels/test_replayssm_teacher_decode_equivalence_gdn.py`. Because the delta-rule recurrence is path-independent, the chunked prefill kernel (`chunk_gated_delta_rule`, the path the model runs at prefill) and step-by-step decode must give the same per-position outputs and final state. Both the baseline and the ReplaySSM step decoders are anchored on the chunked-prefill teacher, whose inputs are built with the same shared `fused_post_conv_prep` the model uses.

Metadata-builder unit tests live in `tests/v1/attention/test_gdn_metadata_builder.py`. The per-row write position and flush flag are the riskiest new logic, so they are covered on CPU with no model: fresh decode, flush boundary, buffer wrap, resume re-anchor after preemption, and per-row independence across a batch. Align mode adds the block re-anchor, the forced boundary flush, and a buffer length that does not divide the mamba block size. Two cases pin the batch split: a final single-token prefill chunk stays in the decode group so a full cudagraph replays with a refreshed cursor, and a first-token prefill stays a prefill. One case asserts the builder rejects stochastic rounding.

Engine-level parity lives in `tests/v1/e2e/test_replayssm_decode.py`. It compares the baseline (feature off) against ReplaySSM (feature on) with greedy decode and `check_logprobs_close` on Qwen3.5-4B, at TP1 and, under `@multi_gpu_test`, at TP2.

On current main, the two kernel files are 92 passed (one H100), and the builder file is 79 passed on CPU (17 ReplaySSM cases; the rest are main's). TP1 and TP2 engine parity both pass for decode and align-mode prefix caching; the TP2 run confirms the per-rank sharded caches and checkpoint stay correct.

```
pytest tests/kernels/test_replayssm_standard_decode_gdn.py \
       tests/kernels/test_replayssm_teacher_decode_equivalence_gdn.py \
       tests/v1/attention/test_gdn_metadata_builder.py \
       tests/v1/e2e/test_replayssm_decode.py -q
```

## Model evaluation (GSM8K)

Evaluated on Qwen3.5-4B (1x H100), greedy, fp32 SSM state, CUDA graphs on, with the `<think>` block disabled in the chat template (`chat_template_kwargs={"enable_thinking": False}`). Accuracy is reported under CoT prompting. Baseline and ReplaySSM use the identical prompt and seed, so the parity comparison is unaffected by the prompt choice.

CoT prompt (verbatim; `{question}` is the GSM8K problem):

```
{question}

Solve step by step, then give the final answer as 'The answer is <number>.'
```

Answer extraction: the number following an `answer is`, `answer:`, `####`, or `\boxed{}` marker (last match), falling back to the last number in the output.

| config | accuracy (CoT, N=1319) |
|---|---:|
| baseline (no ReplaySSM) | 0.917 +/- 0.008 |
| ReplaySSM (L=16) | 0.920 +/- 0.008 |

The 0.003 difference is within one binomial standard error, so ReplaySSM matches the baseline.

Prefix caching (align): on a 20-shot CoT run (N=200) with `--enable-prefix-caching --mamba-cache-mode align`, `get_metrics()` reports a prefix-cache hit rate of 0.90 for the baseline and 0.86 for ReplaySSM, and accuracy is 0.925 for both. The align cached path is also covered by the e2e test `test_replayssm_prefix_caching_matches_baseline`, which asserts cache hits.

## Duplicate check

No open PR addresses ReplaySSM GDN standard decode. This PR is split from the large draft PR [#47576](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/47576) (also closed when the source fork was deleted), and builds on the Mamba2 standard-decode sub-PR [#48018](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48018). The related prior ReplaySSM PRs we are aware of are Mamba2-focused and do not cover GDN:

- [#43102](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/43102) and [#43439](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/43439), earlier PRs from our collaborator on the same ReplaySSM effort. This is the newer, more complete version.
- [#46239](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/46239), opened by another contributor based on our original fork. We have since made substantial changes, intend to land the feature ourselves, and have notified the author.

## Out of scope

- Stochastic rounding for low precision state.
- Speculative decode for GDN, which will land in a later sub-PR.
- Model Runner V2. Like the Mamba2 Triton path on main, GDN ReplaySSM requires `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0`.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Distributed]  Gate MNNVL allreduce workspace creation on fabric support
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Fixes #51986.

On IB-only multi-node topologies, FlashInfer mnnvl workspace creation hangs ~30s and leaks GPU memory. vLLM resolves the `auto` backend to an explicit `"mnnvl"` before calling `create_allreduce_fusion_workspace()`, so FlashInfer's own capability vote (auto path only) never runs, and the existing `mc_ptr` check runs only after the doomed creation attempt. Full analysis in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/51986#issuecomment-5380074578.

This PR gates mnnvl workspace creation on a collective capability probe:

- groups confined to one node keep working via node-local handle exchange (no fabric needed), checked with `in_the_same_node_as()`
- node-spanning groups vote `is_mnnvl_fabric_supported()` across ranks via `all_ranks_support_mnnvl()`; a rank whose local probe fails still joins the vote to keep the collective symmetric
- the result is latched per group so the per-layer workspace retry path doesn't repeat NVML probes and object allgathers
- older flashinfer without the probe APIs falls back to the pre-existing attempt-and-check behavior

When the vote is negative the workspace getter returns `None`, so `AllReduceFusionPass` disables itself and the unfused allreduce + rmsnorm path is kept, avoiding the hang and the leak.

Note: distinct from #48075 (single-node bridged NVLink where creation succeeds and the crash happens later) and from #53253, which gates the `CustomAllreduce` symmetric-memory rendezvous on pre-Blackwell cross-node groups. This PR is about the FlashInfer allreduce fusion workspace path.

## Test Plan

- Unit test for the new capability gate (mocked probe results)
- Manual: multi-node IB-only setup, verify no hang at pass init and fusion pass disabled cleanly

## Test Result

- Unit tests pass: gate returns `False` on mocked IB-only topology, workspace creation is skipped and `get_fi_ar_workspace()` returns `None`
- Verified on a 2-node IB-only setup (2x8 B300): no hang at pass init (previously ~30s x2), `AllReduceFusionPass` disables itself cleanly with a log message, no residual GPU memory from failed allocation

## AI assistance
This change was implemented with AI (Claude Code CLI) assistance; all changes were reviewed and tested by the human submitter.

commits.pr_title: [MoE] Use sorted fused-MoE path on integrated GPUs for multi-token batches (#63943)
commits.pr_body:
## Summary

Triton fused MoE currently engages the low-latency unpermuted "naive block assignment" path when `num_tokens * top_k * 4 <= global_num_experts`, bypassing `moe_align_block_size`.

- **On discrete HBM GPUs (A100, H100, B200):** This yields a ~12–19% decode speedup at `M=2..4` by eliminating the fixed CUDA launch overhead of the alignment kernel.
- **On integrated/unified-memory GPUs (NVIDIA GB10 / DGX Spark with UMA LPDDR5x):** Multiple tokens routing to identical experts cause redundant weight reads over shared memory bandwidth, leading to an 8% to 52% decode regression (#63943).

This PR introduces an adaptive, architecture-aware threshold:
1. **Integrated / UMA GPUs (`current_platform.is_integrated_gpu()`):** Restricts naive assignment strictly to `num_tokens == 1` where expert collision is impossible, routing multi-token batches (`M >= 2`) through the sorted `moe_align_block_size` path.
2. **Discrete GPUs:** Preserves the existing `num_tokens * top_k * 4 <= global_num_experts` heuristic.

> **Hardware Scope:** Measured on NVIDIA GB10 (DGX Spark) only; other integrated GPUs such as Jetson Thor take the same path but are unmeasured.

Fixes #63943.

## Test Plan

1. **Unit tests in `tests/kernels/moe/test_moe.py`:**
   - `test_integrated_gpu_expert_assignment`: Parameterized across `M in [1, 2, 4, 8]` for both integrated and discrete GPUs, verifying integrated GPUs take sorted path at `M >= 2` while taking naive path at `M=1`, and discrete GPUs preserve naive path at `M <= 4`.
   - `test_host_resident_weights_take_sorted_path`: Verifies zero regression on host-resident weights (#62054).

2. **GB10 Hardware Validation (by @ks-huang):**
   Evaluated on NVIDIA GB10 (sm_121, `is_integrated = 1`) with Qwen3-30B-A3B BF16, TP=1, `--moe-backend triton`, greedy decode (128 tokens):
   - **CUDA Graphs (`FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`):**
     - Batch 1: 31.1 ms/step (unchanged)
     - Batch 4 (4 different prompts): 73.7 ms -> 67.2 ms (**-8.8%**)
     - Batch 4 (4 identical prompts): 65.8 ms -> 29.7 ms (**-55.0%**)
   - **Eager Mode:**
     - Batch 1: 32.8 ms/step (unchanged)
     - Batch 4 (different prompts): 75.3 ms -> 69.1 ms (**-8.2%**)
     - Batch 4 (identical prompts): 67.3 ms -> 32.4 ms (**-52.0%**)
   - Output text is identical to stock in all runs.

3. **A100 Discrete Baseline Microbenchmark:**
   Verified on NVIDIA A100-PCIE-40GB (`E=128`, `top_k=8`) that naive path remains ~19% faster at `M=2` even under 100% expert collision due to dedicated HBM bandwidth absorbing redundant reads.

   | M (batch) | Scenario | Naive (µs) | Grouped (µs) | Delta |
   |---|---|---|---|---|
   | 1 | Independent | 345.5 | 428.5 | **+19.4% (Naive)** |
   | 1 | Shared Experts (100% collision) | 344.0 | 427.4 | **+19.5% (Naive)** |
   | 2 | Independent | 342.1 | 423.6 | **+19.3% (Naive)** |
   | 2 | Shared Experts (100% collision) | 345.4 | 426.1 | **+18.9% (Naive)** |
   | 4 | Independent | 399.2 | 427.1 | **+6.5% (Naive)** |
   | 4 | Shared Experts (100% collision) | 377.1 | 428.7 | **+12.0% (Naive)** |
   | 8 | Independent | 597.7 | 598.3 | **+0.1% (Tie)** |
   | 8 | Shared Experts (100% collision) | 424.1 | 422.3 | **-0.4% (Tie)** |

   <details>
   <summary>A100 Benchmark Script (Standalone Reproduction)</summary>

   ```python
   import torch
   from vllm.config import VllmConfig, set_current_vllm_config
   import vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.fused_moe as fused_moe_module
   from tests.kernels.moe.utils import fused_moe

   def benchmark_latency(fn, warmup=50, iters=200):
       for _ in range(warmup):
           fn()
       torch.cuda.synchronize()
       start = torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True)
       end = torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True)
       start.record()
       for _ in range(iters):
           fn()
       end.record()
       torch.cuda.synchronize()
       return (start.elapsed_time(end) / iters) * 1000.0

   def run_suite():
       vllm_config = VllmConfig()
       device = "cuda:0"
       dtype = torch.bfloat16
       e, topk, k, n = 128, 8, 2048, 1024

       torch.manual_seed(42)
       torch.cuda.manual_seed(42)
       w1 = torch.randn((e, 2 * n, k), device=device, dtype=dtype) / 8
       w2 = torch.randn((e, k, n), device=device, dtype=dtype) / 8

       orig_align = fused_moe_module.moe_align_block_size
       orig_prep = fused_moe_module._prepare_expert_assignment

       def forced_grouped_prep(*args, **kwargs):
           topk_ids = args[0] if len(args) > 0 else kwargs['topk_ids']
           config = args[1] if len(args) > 1 else kwargs['config']
           global_num_experts = args[4] if len(args) > 4 else kwargs['global_num_experts']
           expert_map = args[5] if len(args) > 5 else kwargs['expert_map']
           ignore_invalid = kwargs.get('ignore_invalid_experts', False)
           return orig_align(topk_ids, config["BLOCK_SIZE_M"], global_num_experts, expert_map, ignore_invalid_experts=ignore_invalid)

       for m in [1, 2, 4, 8]:
           for scenario in ["Independent", "Shared Experts"]:
               a = torch.randn((m, k), device=device, dtype=dtype)
               score = torch.randn((m, e), device=device, dtype=dtype) if scenario == "Independent" else torch.randn((1, e), device=device, dtype=dtype).repeat(m, 1)

               fused_moe_module._prepare_expert_assignment = orig_prep
               with set_current_vllm_config(vllm_config):
                   time_naive = benchmark_latency(lambda: fused_moe(a, w1, w2, score, topk, renormalize=False))

               fused_moe_module._prepare_expert_assignment = forced_grouped_prep
               with set_current_vllm_config(vllm_config):
                   time_grouped = benchmark_latency(lambda: fused_moe(a, w1, w2, score, topk, renormalize=False))

               fused_moe_module._prepare_expert_assignment = orig_prep
               diff_pct = ((time_grouped - time_naive) / time_grouped) * 100.0
               print(f"M={m} | {scenario:<14} | Naive: {time_naive:.1f}us | Grouped: {time_grouped:.1f}us | {diff_pct:+.1f}%")

   if __name__ == "__main__":
       run_suite()
   ```
   </details>

commits.pr_title: [HiSparse] Reuse finished requests' GPU copies before cached prefixes
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Fixes #68725.

When a request finishes, HiSparse keeps its clean resident pages in the GPU pool as copies. They go to the free-queue tail, at the same LRU priority as prefix-cached indexer blocks. That ordering is the bug:

- A host prefix hit needs the GPU indexer blocks; a copy only speeds up a hit that also finds them.
- A long request leaves about 1 indexer block and several resident copies per page.
- Later requests' copies therefore outlive earlier prefixes' indexer blocks, and re-sent prompts miss far below host-pool capacity.

The fix adds `BlockPool.deprioritize_blocks`, which moves free blocks into a middle tier of the free queue: after uncached blocks, before prefix-cached ones. `FreeKVCacheBlockQueue` tracks its first cached block, so the move is O(1). HiSparse deprioritizes copies that no live request reads, page by page across resident groups. Allocation therefore takes uncached free blocks first, then deprioritized copies, then prefix-cached blocks.

P/D decoders reach the same loss a second way: promoting an imported prefix's host pages into GPU resident pages counted every free block as spare, prefix-cached indexer blocks included. Promotion now takes only blocks that hold no cached prefix, meaning the free queue's leading uncached run, which includes deprioritized copies.

Alternatives considered:

- **Copies at the queue head** (`evict_first`). This fixes the loss, but every copy dies at the next allocation, so copy reuse drops to zero.
- **Splicing copies in before the first cached block by walking the queue** (as the umbp connector's `_free_to_cached_front` does). Same order, but each splice walks the leading uncached run: 12.6 ms at 150k free blocks.

Copy page hits when a prompt is re-sent, in a 10k-block simulation:

| Re-send lag | main | head | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2 requests | 4720 | 0 | 4720 |
| 10 requests | 4400 | 0 | 3528 |

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py -k hisparse
pytest tests/v1/core/
```

`test_hisparse_finished_copies_do_not_evict_older_prefix` and `test_hisparse_import_promotion_keeps_cached_prefixes` fail without their fixes and pass here. `test_hisparse_prefix_hit_adopts_gpu_shadow_pages` now drains the pool after adopting a deprioritized copy and checks every block is handed out once. `tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py` covers the queue's cached-head tracking.

## Test Result

**Unit tests**
- HiSparse tests pass.
- `tests/v1/core/` has the same set of failures as main. All are CPU-runner environment failures, such as no spec decode without Triton.

**Simulation** (scheduler + coordinator with a 10k-block GPU pool and 14k-block host pool): send a 60-page prefix, then 40 different 60-page requests, then re-send the prefix.
- main: 0 of 56 pages hit.
- this PR: 56 of 56 pages hit.

**Repro on main**, 8×B200, NVFP4 HiSparse model from the issue (TP8 single-node, and 4+4 multi-node TP), using the issue's probe of 40 × 61.5k-token fillers:
- With `OffloadingConnector`, prefix hits stay at 100% in both topologies.
- With DSpark k=3 added, hits drop to 0%: CPU→GPU traffic is 0 and GPU→CPU traffic is 114 GB. Under HiSparse, the connector offloads only indexer groups, while the DSpark draft groups stay GPU-only and bound the loadable prefix. Offload therefore cannot rescue the prefix once the GPU evicts it; this PR fixes the GPU eviction itself.

**This PR on GPU**: same model and probe as the repro above, with the fix applied on the issue's commit.

| Config | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| 8×B200 TP8, HiSparse + DSpark k=3, no offload | 0 / 61511 tokens (0%) | 61504 / 61511 tokens (100%) |
| 2×(4×B200) multi-node TP8, HiSparse + DSpark k=3 + `OffloadingConnector` (the issue's launch) | 0 / 61479 tokens (0%) | 61504 / 61511 tokens (100%) |

commits.pr_title: [Transformers backend] Migrate InternLM3, IQuestCoder, EXAONE 3 and GPT-J
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Move InternLM3 and IQuestCoder from vLLM's Llama implementation, EXAONE 3 from vLLM's `exaone.py` (deleted) and GPT-J from vLLM's `gpt_j.py` (deleted) to the Transformers modeling backend, following #59679. TeleChat2 and TeleChat3 were dropped from this PR: #67035 removes them.

**Blocked on** huggingface/transformers#50578 (InternLM3) and huggingface/transformers#50579 (IQuestCoder), which add these models to Transformers, with huggingface/transformers#50555 for the tokenizers, and on Transformers 5.24 for huggingface/transformers#50966 (EXAONE 3) and huggingface/transformers#50965 (GPT-J), both merged. Merge once vLLM allows a Transformers release that contains them: `requirements/common.txt` currently caps `transformers < 5.24.0`. The InternLM3/IQuestCoder test entries require `5.23.0` and the EXAONE/GPT-J ones `5.24.0`; update them if they land in a later release.

## Claims

- `InternLM3ForCausalLM` and `IQuestCoderForCausalLM` → `TransformersForCausalLM`. Both were registry aliases of `LlamaForCausalLM`, so they only need registry changes.
- `ExaoneForCausalLM` (EXAONE 3.0, 3.5, Deep) → `TransformersForCausalLM`, and `exaone.py` is deleted. huggingface/transformers#50966 loads the checkpoints into the Llama classes through a conversion mapping, which the backend already applies when loading weights.
- `GPTJForCausalLM` → `TransformersForCausalLM`, and `gpt_j.py` is deleted. huggingface/transformers#50965 moves GPT-J onto the attention interface with TP and PP plans. LoRA is now supported too.
- GPT-J's attention module is itself named `attn`, so the backend's `Attention` lives at `attn.attn`. The rule #65949 added to native GPT-J (#65945: compressed-tensors FP8 KV-cache scales silently dropped) moves into the backend as `NESTED_ATTN_SCALE_MAPPER`, applied to any model whose attention module is named `attn`. Its unit test now targets the backend rule.
- **No `--trust-remote-code` needed.** huggingface/transformers#50578, huggingface/transformers#50579 and huggingface/transformers#50555 also load these checkpoints' tokenizers natively, so model, config and tokenizer all come from Transformers. The test entries no longer set `trust_remote_code`.
- gsm8k accuracy and throughput match `main` within run-to-run noise.
- Docs rows move into the "supported via the Transformers modeling backend" table.

## Validation

1x B200 per model. `main` (c3a347a548) vs this branch's first revision, in the same environment: Transformers with the model PRs (`5.23.0.dev0`), `--trust-remote-code` (needed on `main`), auto dtype. The server logs confirm every branch run uses the Transformers modeling backend and no `main` run does.

| Model | gsm8k `main` | gsm8k branch | Output tok/s `main` | Output tok/s branch |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `internlm/internlm3-8b-instruct` | 0.697 | 0.691 | 12,817 | 13,175 |
| `IQuestLab/IQuest-Coder-V1-7B-Instruct` (2 runs each) | 0.556, 0.553 | 0.541, 0.560 | 15,752, 15,772 | 15,256, 15,652 |

Without `--trust-remote-code` (the latest revision, which tokenizes natively; same environment and commands minus the flag):

| Model | gsm8k | Greedy vs Transformers (3 chat prompts, same prompt ids) |
|---|---|---|
| `internlm/internlm3-8b-instruct` | 0.696 | 2/3 identical, 1 diverges at token 18 |
| `IQuestLab/IQuest-Coder-V1-7B-Instruct` | 0.563 | 3/3 identical |

EXAONE 3 (1x B200, `main` 1ae1b64807 vs this branch, same environment): huggingface/transformers#50966 applied to the commit before huggingface/transformers#50585 (see Details), no `--trust-remote-code` on either side (on `main`, `exaone.py` reads the native `ExaoneConfig` through its `attribute_map`), `--max-model-len 4096`. The server logs show `ExaoneForCausalLM` on `main` and `TransformersForCausalLM` on the branch, with the same attention backend.

| Model | gsm8k `main` | gsm8k branch | Output tok/s `main` | Output tok/s branch |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `LGAI-EXAONE/EXAONE-3.5-2.4B-Instruct` | 0.654 | 0.657 | 17,689 | 17,690 |
| `LGAI-EXAONE/EXAONE-3.0-7.8B-Instruct` | 0.791 | 0.792 | 11,450 | 11,472 |

The server logs show `trust_remote_code=False` and the Transformers modeling backend for both.

GPT-J (1x B200, `main` 1ae1b64807 vs that commit plus this PR's GPT-J commit, both with #68717 applied and the same build artifacts; Transformers `main` cf0fd5eea0, `--max-model-len 2048 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.35` because the GPU was shared). The server logs show `GPTJForCausalLM` on `main` and `TransformersForCausalLM` on the branch. GPT-J 6B is a 2021 base model, so gsm8k only checks that both sides agree.

| Model | gsm8k `main` | gsm8k branch | Output tok/s `main` | Output tok/s branch |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `EleutherAI/gpt-j-6b` | 0.036 | 0.037 | 6,437 | 6,426 |

Other cells in the first table are one run each. IQuest's first gsm8k run differed by 0.015 (about 1σ for 1319 questions), so I repeated it on both sides. The repeats overlap, so the gap was noise.

gsm8k (5-shot, 1319 questions):

```bash
vllm serve <model> --port 8200 --trust-remote-code --max-model-len 8192 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.6
python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8200
```

Throughput:

```bash
vllm bench throughput --model <model> --trust-remote-code \
  --max-model-len 8192 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.6 \
  --input-len 1024 --output-len 256 --num-prompts 1000
```

With `--trust-remote-code`, greedy generation through `LLM(...)` exactly matched greedy generation with Transformers for InternLM3.

Tests on the latest revision (B200, with `min_transformers_version` temporarily lowered to `5.23.0.dev0` so they don't skip; `test_initialization` now runs without `trust_remote_code`):

```bash
pytest tests/models/test_initialization.py -k "InternLM3ForCausalLM or IQuestCoderForCausalLM"  # 2 passed
pytest tests/models/test_registry.py  # 471 passed, 3 skipped, 1 failed: KananaV needs timm, not installed
pytest tests/model_executor/test_weight_utils.py -k TestKvCacheScaleMapper  # 23 passed in 2.81s (local, includes the GPT-J cases against the backend rule)
pytest tests/models/test_registry.py -k "GPTJ or Exaone"  # 8 passed in 1.82s (local)
```

## Details

- **`--trust-remote-code` gets the remote code:** the checkpoints still carry an `auto_map`, so passing the flag loads the repos' v4-era remote code (which fails under Transformers v5, e.g. InternLM3's `cannot import name 'LossKwargs'`), as for any other model. Without the flag, model, config and tokenizer all come from Transformers.
- **InternLM3, IQuestCoder:** Transformers maps them to its Llama classes, with only their configs specific to them. InternLM3 generates the same tokens as before (3/3 prompts).
- **Tokenizers:** their `tokenizer_config.json` names classes that only exist in the repos' remote code, so on `main` they need `--trust-remote-code`, which vLLM can't enable for the tokenizer alone. The model PRs and huggingface/transformers#50555 load them natively from `tokenizer.model`. Encoding matches the remote tokenizers exactly for InternLM3, except for remote-code bugs on literal special-token strings. For IQuestCoder, about 96% of texts match: 11,859 of its pieces share the top score, and SentencePiece's positional tie-breaking can't be reproduced by `tokenizers` BPE (IQuest's own `tokenizer.json` does no better). Details are in huggingface/transformers#50579.
- **IQuestCoder BOS, fixed without the flag:** under Transformers v5, IQuestCoder's remote tokenizer prepends BOS even though its `tokenizer_config.json` sets `add_bos_token: false` (4.53.2 doesn't). The native tokenizer respects the config. With `--trust-remote-code`, the remote tokenizer and this bug remain, as on `main`.
- **Transformers main broke `vllm serve` on the backend, not specific to this PR:** huggingface/transformers#50585 wraps `LlamaModel.forward` in `@deprecate_kwarg`, and `bytecode_hook` then failed with `KeyError: self` at engine startup. #68717 (merged) fixes it.
- **Duplicate check:** no open PRs or issues touch these models (searched `InternLM3`, `IQuestCoder`, `EXAONE`, `GPT-J`, `gpt_j` and Transformers-backend migrations).

commits.pr_title: [Perf][Parser] Find GLM-4.7 tool-call arguments in linear time
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

`glm47` finds tool-call arguments with `_ARG_RE` and `_PARTIAL_ARG_RE`. For each `<arg_key>` they retry every later `</arg_key>` and scan to the end of the text for each try, so arguments holding unclosed tag text cost cubic time. This finds the tags with `str.find` in one pass and returns the same arguments.

Related: four fixes for the end-of-request stall on long non-streaming outputs - #69500 (lexer), #69636 (single-pass argument deltas), #69637 (`glm47` argument scan), #69638 (detokenizer). Each stands alone. Tracking: #69643.

## Claims

- Finding the arguments of a call costs O(n). A length-capped output that stops inside a call whose value holds tag text (20K tokens repeating `<tool_call>shell<arg_key>command</arg_key><arg_value>ls` with nothing closed) takes 74.4 s to parse on `main`, and 0.09 s with this PR on top of #69500 (0.89 s without it).
- Same results: `_glm47_parse_args` returns the same arguments and open key as the regexes, for whole texts and for texts grown through `_ClosedArgs` as in streaming.
- Non-streaming chat, Messages and Responses requests run this parse and `count_reasoning_tokens` on the API server's event loop, so the cost stalls every request on that server. Streaming conversions call the same function.
- No config, flag or API change.

## Validation

| Check | Command | `main` `1fd30e4f6e` | This PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| Parser suites | `pytest tests/parser tests/tool_parsers tests/reasoning --ignore=tests/parser/mistral/test_tool_calls.py --ignore=tests/parser/test_harmony.py` | `9711 passed, 1 skipped, 30 xfailed, 384 subtests passed` | `9711 passed, 1 skipped, 30 xfailed, 384 subtests passed` |
| Parity | random texts from the four argument tags, tag fragments, Unicode and ASCII-only whitespace (`\xa0`, `\u2003`, `\x1c`) and filler, `partial` true and false, plus random prefixes fed in order through one `_ClosedArgs`; params, key order, open key and cache state compared with the regex version, 3 seeds | | 442,000 of 442,000 identical |
| Differential, `glm47`/`glm45` | 6,000 structured outputs (reasoning, calls with stray and repeated tags, missing closers, random truncation): `parse`, `count_reasoning_tokens`, and a streamed run with random chunking | | identical |

`test_closed_pairs_are_parsed_once` counted `_ARG_RE.finditer` matches and now counts the pairs `_closed_args` yields, with the same assertion.

Suites ran on CPU in `vllm-ci-postmerge-repo:267c0656410d6a01c1e2f4f0bf9bad996a195673-arm64-cpu` with the tree on `PYTHONPATH`. The ignored files fail collection in that image on both trees (mistral-common version, harmony download).

End-of-request parse with `ParserManager.get_parser("glm47", "glm45")` and the `zai-org/GLM-4.7` tokenizer, Apple M4 Pro, same image. Before = `main` + #69500, after = `main` + #69500 + this PR (without #69500 the lexer's own quadratic cost hides the change above 20K tokens). Before at 40K tokens took 590 s in a separate run, so larger sizes were not run:

| output | tokens | before parse s | after parse s | before count s | after count s |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| unclosed argument with tags | 4995 | 1.24 | 0.02 | 1.24 | 0.02 |
| unclosed argument with tags | 9995 | 9.28 | 0.05 | 9.34 | 0.15 |
| unclosed argument with tags | 19995 | 71.83 | 0.09 | 71.74 | 0.21 |
| unclosed argument with tags | 39995 | not run | 0.19 | not run | 0.48 |
| unclosed argument with tags | 79995 | not run | 0.48 | not run | 0.94 |
| unclosed argument with tags | 159995 | not run | 0.98 | not run | 2.68 |

<details>
<summary>Benchmark script</summary>

```python
"""Time the end-of-request parse of one long output with the glm47 tool and glm45 reasoning parsers.

A non-streaming chat, Messages or Responses request ends with `parser.parse(output.text)` and
`parser.count_reasoning_tokens(token_ids)`. This times both on outputs that repeat one unit until the output holds
N tokens. Nothing after the repeats closes, as in an output cut off by `max_tokens`.

usage: python bench_parse_shapes.py --tokenizer <dir> --shapes a,b [--sizes 20000,40000,80000,160000]
"""
import argparse
import time

from vllm.entrypoints.openai.chat_completion.protocol import ChatCompletionRequest
from vllm.parser import ParserManager
from vllm.tokenizers import get_tokenizer

ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
ap.add_argument("--tokenizer", required=True)
ap.add_argument("--shapes", required=True)
ap.add_argument("--sizes", default="20000,40000,80000,160000")
a = ap.parse_args()

S = {"type": "string"}
TOOLS = [
    {"type": "function", "function": {"name": "shell", "parameters": {
        "type": "object", "properties": {"command": {"type": "array", "items": S}}, "required": ["command"]}}},
    {"type": "function", "function": {"name": "edit", "parameters": {
        "type": "object", "properties": {"path": S, "old": S, "new": S}, "required": ["path", "old", "new"]}}},
]
HEAD = "Checking.</think>"
EDIT = HEAD + "<tool_call>edit<arg_key>path</arg_key><arg_value>a.py</arg_value>"
SHAPES = {
    # One call that repeats closed argument pairs.
    "repeated argument pairs": (EDIT, "<arg_key>old</arg_key><arg_value>x = 0</arg_value>"
                                      "<arg_key>new</arg_key><arg_value>x = 1</arg_value>"),
    # Reasoning that quotes a tool call, so the first quote opens a call that never closes.
    "tool call quoted in reasoning": ("", "It should be <tool_call>edit<arg_key>old</arg_key>"
                                          "<arg_value>x</arg_value> here.\n"),
    # One call whose argument value never closes and holds tag text.
    "unclosed argument with tags": (HEAD, "<tool_call>shell<arg_key>command</arg_key><arg_value>ls\n"),
    "repeated tool calls": (HEAD, '<tool_call>shell<arg_key>command</arg_key><arg_value>["ls"]</arg_value>'
                                  "</tool_call>"),
}

tok = get_tokenizer(a.tokenizer)
cls = ParserManager.get_parser(tool_parser_name="glm47", reasoning_parser_name="glm45", enable_auto_tools=True)
req = ChatCompletionRequest(model="m", messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "x"}], tools=TOOLS, tool_choice="auto")
print("| output | tokens | parse s | count_reasoning_tokens s |")
print("|---|---|---|---|")
for name in a.shapes.split(","):
    prefix, unit = SHAPES[name]
    unit_ids = tok.encode(unit, add_special_tokens=False)
    pre_ids = tok.encode(prefix, add_special_tokens=False) if prefix else []
    for n in [int(s) for s in a.sizes.split(",")]:
        ids = pre_ids + unit_ids * max(1, (n - len(pre_ids)) // len(unit_ids))
        text = tok.decode(ids, skip_special_tokens=False)
        parser = cls(tok, req.tools, chat_template_kwargs={}, model_config=None)
        t0 = time.perf_counter()
        parser.parse(text, req, enable_auto_tools=True, model_output_token_ids=ids)
        t1 = time.perf_counter()
        parser.count_reasoning_tokens(ids)
        t2 = time.perf_counter()
        print(f"| {name} | {len(ids)} | {t1 - t0:.2f} | {t2 - t1:.2f} |", flush=True)
```

</details>

## Details

For a match starting at an `<arg_key>`, the key runs to the first `</arg_key>` followed by `\s*<arg_value>` whose value has a closing `</arg_value>` after it. A later `</arg_key>` or a later `<arg_key>` can only move the value start further right, so when the first candidate has no closing tag, no other match exists. `_find_arg` relies on that: it takes the first `<arg_key>` from `pos`, walks `</arg_key>` occurrences until one is followed by `<arg_value>`, and stops. `_closed_args` adds the `</arg_value>` lookup and replaces `_ARG_RE.finditer`, and the open trailing value of `_PARTIAL_ARG_RE` is the rest of the text from the value start. `\s*` keeps the `regex` module's definition through `_VALUE_START_RE`, an anchored match that only reads the whitespace run.

#54971 changes the key pattern so a stray `arg_key` tag cannot enter the key. If both land, that rule becomes a check on the key span in `_find_arg`.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Don't report sibling cache hits in n>1 prefill stats
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

**goal:** an `n>1` request reports prefix cache usage the way an `n=1` request does.

**scope:** only the per-request value is wrong: `RequestOutput.num_cached_tokens` offline, and `usage.prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens` online with `--enable-prompt-tokens-details`. prometheus metrics are unaffected: they record one `num_cached_tokens` per sampled output.

**context:** the `n` children share the prompt, so later children hit the kv blocks their sibling just wrote. non-streaming responses took `cached_tokens` from the last child to finish: a cold `n=4` request reported 1,216 of 1,230 prompt tokens as cached (streaming reported 0).

## Claims

- `RequestState.observe_prefill` records each child's prefill stats and hands them to `ParentRequest`, which keeps the stats (`num_cached_tokens`, `num_cache_creation_tokens`) of the child with the fewest cached tokens, i.e. what was cached before the request. children with no prefill stats (failed before prefill) are skipped.
- `RequestOutput` reports those stats. `FinishedRequestStats` still records each child's own count (#56361).

## Validation

- `test_parallel_sampling_num_cached_tokens` (new, gpu): at 230ad0e on a100, `pytest tests/v1/engine/test_llm_engine.py -k parallel_sampling`: `3 passed, 12 deselected, 3 warnings in 110.78s`. with main's `output_processor.py` + `parallel_sampling.py` swapped in: `assert 112 == 0` (`1 failed, 14 deselected, 1 warning in 21.05s`). earlier it also failed on main at 64-token blocks (`64 == 0`) and passed here.
- a100, llama-3.1-8b, vllm main 4527515cd, cold `/v1/completions`, 2 trials: `cached_tokens` at `n`=2/4/8 is 1216–1264 on main, 0 here. warm `n=4` = warm `n=1` = 1248. chat completions: same. re-checked at cb50988 on 64-token blocks: cold 0 at every `n`, streaming and not; warm `n=4` = warm `n=1` = 1216.
- at 230ad0e (main 28fb136 merged, its precompiled wheel): `pytest tests/v1/engine/test_output_processor.py`: `61 passed in 459.54s (0:07:39)`, with the tokenizer fixture and `test_stop_token`'s name check pointed at the ungated mirror `unsloth/Llama-3.2-1B` locally (`meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B` is gated for me). `pytest tests/v1/engine/test_parallel_sampling.py`: `3 passed in 1.91s`. pre-commit passes.

## Details

- the minimum can undercount only if blocks are evicted between siblings, never overcount. preemption doesn't change it: prefill stats are recorded at first scheduling only.
- the failed-before-prefill child has no test of its own (review: too niche for one).
- not a duplicate: #55120 (multi-prompt requests), #56361 (prometheus metrics).
- ai-assisted (metamate). i reviewed every line and ran the tests.

commits.pr_title: [Transformers backend] Apply checkpoint conversions that split a tensor
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

The Transformers backend now applies checkpoint `WeightConverter`s whose operations only split one tensor (`Chunk`/`Split`), such as a fused `query_key_value` into `q_proj`/`k_proj`/`v_proj`. Split out of #68728, which needs it for `sarvamai/sarvam-30b`.

## Claims

- A `WeightConverter` with one source pattern and only `Chunk`/`Split` operations is applied to the weights with Transformers' own ops, and the pieces then load through the existing renamings and fusions. Before, only `WeightRenaming`s were applied, so such checkpoints failed to load.
- Other `WeightConverter`s (merges, transposes, ...) are still ignored, as on `main`.

## Validation

**Unit test** (new, in the existing `test_backend.py`), run on the PR head:

```bash
pytest -q tests/models/transformers/test_backend.py -k split_weights
```

```text
# main's transformers/base.py
E   ImportError: cannot import name 'SplitWeights' from 'vllm.model_executor.models.transformers.base'
14 warnings, 1 error in 0.11s
# this PR
1 passed, 46 deselected, 14 warnings in 0.60s
```

**End to end**: no Transformers backend model on `main` has a split-only converter (Transformers' `nomic_bert` and `gte` do, but fail earlier on `main`, see Details), so this uses `sarvamai/sarvam-30b` through #68728 with and without this change (without: `d7b856cf48`; with: this PR's `ce63ea3e5e` plus #68728's registry entry). 1x B200, Transformers `main` (`ab19734bb`):

```python
llm = LLM(model="sarvamai/sarvam-30b", max_model_len=2048, gpu_memory_utilization=0.6, enforce_eager=True)
llm.chat([{"role": "user", "content": "What is the capital of France? Answer in one sentence."}],
         SamplingParams(max_tokens=64, temperature=0))
```

```text
# without this change
ValueError: There is no module or parameter named 'model.layers.0.self_attn.query_key_value' in TransformersMoEForCausalLM.
RuntimeError: Engine core initialization failed. See root cause above. Failed core proc(s): {}

# with this change
INFO [moe.py:444] Fused: gate + experts + shared experts (Glm4MoeMoE) -> MoERunner (internal routing)
OUTPUT: '<think>1.  **Analyze the user\'s request:**\n    *   **Question:** "What is the capital of France?"\n    *   **Constraint 1:** "Answer in one sentence."\n    *   **Constraint 2 (implicit):** The answer must be correct.\n\n2.  '
# native SarvamMoEForCausalLM (`main`, `--trust-remote-code` for its config)
OUTPUT: '<think>1.  **Analyze the user\'s request:**\n    *   **Question:** "What is the capital of France?"\n    *   **Constraint:** "Answer in one sentence."\n\n2.  **Identify the core information needed:**\n    *   The capital of France is Paris. This is'
```

Greedy outputs drift apart after a few lines in bf16, as they do between two runs of `main` on this host; Sarvam-30B's gsm8k through the backend is in #68728.

**Existing backend tests** (`pytest -q tests/models/transformers/test_backend.py`, 2x B200, Transformers 5.22): the same 6 tests fail on this PR and on its base `eb42ba633e` (OLMoE, `test_mla`, two `test_distributed`, two `test_quantization`) from this host's toolchain: precompiled kernels fail with `cudaErrorUnsupportedPtxVersion` and FlashInfer's JIT with `Ninja build failed`, and everything else passes, including both `test_pooling` cases (rerun on a free GPU after another job took memory during the first run).

## Details

- **Fused targets:** `Split` sizes each piece from the target parameter, which the backend may already have replaced (e.g. fused `q_proj`/`k_proj`/`v_proj` into `qkv_proj`), so each `SplitWeights` (one per converter) records the parameter shapes when the mapper is built and resolves names with the mapper from before vLLM's fusions are added.
- **Matching:** converters are matched with Transformers' own `WeightConverter.rename_source_key`, so they match whole names only, respect `scope_prefix` and rename the first occurrence, as Transformers does.
- **Quantized checkpoints:** a quantization tensor stored next to a fused weight (e.g. `query_key_value.weight_scale`) matches the converter too, but has no matching tensor in the model, so it raises a clear error instead of crashing or loading only the first piece.
- **Order:** converters are matched against the checkpoint names before the renamings, while Transformers renames first. No current mapping has a converter whose source only exists after a renaming; applying the renamings inside `SplitWeights` would rename the output twice, which is not safe for every `WeightRenaming` subclass.
- **Version:** `Split` only exists from Transformers 5.22, above vLLM's 5.16 floor, so the ops are matched by class name for now (with a TODO to use `isinstance` once the floor reaches 5.22).
- **Encoders:** `nomic_bert` and `gte` have split-only converters too, but the backend cannot serve them yet: their attention modules have no `layer_idx`, so it fails with `Layer 0 does not dispatch through the Transformers attention interface`.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Core] Avoid initializing CUDA while resolving AllReduce+RMSNorm fusion config
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

On Hopper/Blackwell with `tensor_parallel_size > 1` and flashinfer installed, building the engine config initializes CUDA in the calling process. vLLM then sees "CUDA is initialized" and overrides `VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD` from `fork` to `spawn`, which logs a warning on every `LLM()` call and breaks tests that rely on monkeypatching (`tests/v1/shutdown/`).

Addresses item 1 under "Side effects at import time" in #59433.

## Root cause

`PassConfig.default_fi_allreduce_fusion_max_size_mb()` imported the whole `allreduce_rms_fusion` pass module just to read the `FI_ALLREDUCE_FUSION_MAX_SIZE_MB` table. That module imports `flashinfer.comm` at module level, and importing it initializes CUDA. The import direction was backwards: config resolution should not depend on a pass module.

```
create_engine_config() → PassConfig.flashinfer_max_size()
  → default_fi_allreduce_fusion_max_size_mb()
  → import allreduce_rms_fusion → import flashinfer.comm → CUDA initialized
```

## Fix

Move `FI_ALLREDUCE_FUSION_MAX_SIZE_MB` into `vllm/config/compilation.py` and drop the cross-module import. `allreduce_rms_fusion.py` never read the table, and its own flashinfer import is unchanged. Also replace the stale copy of the table in the `PassConfig` docstring with a pointer to the single definition. No runtime logic change.

`tests/standalone_tests/lazy_imports.py` now also asserts that `PassConfig().flashinfer_max_size(2)` does not import the fusion pass module.

## Test Plan

```bash
python3 tests/standalone_tests/lazy_imports.py
cd tests && python3 -m pytest -v --import-mode=append \
    'v1/shutdown/test_forward_error.py::test_async_llm_model_error' \
    'v1/shutdown/test_forward_error.py::test_llm_model_error'
```

## Test Result

GB300 (cc 10.3), upstream nightly image `nightly-40941f2c4` (main), 5 fresh-process runs each:

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `torch.cuda.is_initialized()` after `PassConfig().flashinfer_max_size(2)` | True | False |
| `flashinfer` in `sys.modules` | True | False |
| `PassConfig().flashinfer_max_size(2)` time | 3.3–4.6 s (median ≈3.4 s) | 0.1 ms |
| Modules imported by that call | 2138 | 0 |
| Returned value | 67108864 | 67108864 |
| `create_engine_config()`, TP=2, tiny model, `enforce_eager`, warm cache (median) | 4.3 s | 2.7 s |
| `torch.cuda.is_initialized()` after `create_engine_config()` | True | False |

The new `lazy_imports.py` check fails on main and passes with this change.

On the original branch (before the rebase), the three `tests/v1/shutdown/test_forward_error.py` cases that failed under the forced `spawn` pass, and the spawn warning is gone.

This takes flashinfer off the API server's path only; workers still import it where they need it.

AI assistance: prepared with Claude Code; I reviewed every changed line and ran the measurements above myself.

The compiled requirements were updated in place with pins and hashes from PyPI. Validated by `/ci run nightly` against the `v5.24-release` branch before the release; the only bump-caused failure (Nemotron-Parse) was fixed by huggingface/transformers#51177, now in v5.24.1.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Fail at launch for multimodal models the Rust frontend cannot serve
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

The Rust frontend starts a multimodal model it cannot serve as if it were text-only, then rejects every image request although the engine loaded the vision tower and accepts the media. This PR makes such a start fail at launch with a message that names the way out (`--language-model-only` or `VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=0`). A model the frontend serves only partly starts with a warning, and the per-request error for the unserved modality names the Rust frontend and the options. The Rust CI lane's SmolVLM text-only cases are deselected accordingly.

## Claims

- A model with a multimodal preprocessor config but no Rust processor spec (for example SmolVLM / Idefics3, Qwen2.5-Omni) fails at launch instead of starting and rejecting media per request. With every modality limited to 0 (what Python's `--language-model-only` means), it still loads as text-only.
- A spec that resolves none of the modalities it declares for the checkpoint (modalities limited to 0 do not count) fails at launch the same way.
- A spec that serves some declared modalities but not all (for example `google/gemma-4-E2B-it`: image served, `audio` declared with no audio processor in the `gemma4` spec) starts with a warning. Requests with the unserved modality get an error naming the Rust frontend, `--limit-mm-per-prompt` and `VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=0`, instead of "`audio` input is not supported by this model".
- Text-only models (no spec, no media preprocessor config) and specs that declare nothing for the checkpoint load as before, without the spurious "multimodal model spec is not registered" warning.

## Validation

Rust CI set (`.buildkite/scripts/run-rust-frontend-cargo-ci.sh`) on `613aeec6f0`, based on `92b9817e02`:

```bash
cargo fmt --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --all -- --check                    # clean
cargo sort --workspace --check rust                                           # clean
cargo deny --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --config rust/deny.toml check bans # clean
cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings  # clean
cargo nextest run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-features --locked --no-fail-fast  # 2849 passed, 13 skipped
```

New tests in `vllm-chat` (`multimodal::tests`), each failing with its check disabled and passing with it:
- `multimodal_model_without_spec_fails_launch_unless_media_is_disabled`: no spec plus a media preprocessor config, as a standalone file or as each `processor_config.json` section the Rust processors read, is an error (message snapshot); every limit 0 loads text-only.
- `processor_config_without_media_sections_is_text_only`: a `processor_config.json` without media sections does not count as multimodal.
- `spec_without_resolved_modality_fails_launch_unless_limited_to_zero`: a Qwen3-VL config whose tokenizer has neither placeholder is an error (message snapshot); with image and video limited to 0 it loads text-only.
- `unsupported_declared_modality_is_rejected_per_request`: a Qwen3-VL config declaring video without a `<|video_pad|>` token loads with image only; a video request gets the Rust-frontend error, an audio request (not declared) the existing "not supported by this model" error.

Frontend-only startup (`vllm-rs frontend` up to the engine handshake, release build; the SmolVLM and Gemma 4 rows re-checked on `613aeec6f0` by loading the model backends from the real checkpoints, no engine):

| Model | Result |
|---|---|
| `HuggingFaceTB/SmolVLM-256M-Instruct` | fails (no spec); starts with `--language-model-only` |
| `Qwen/Qwen2.5-Omni-3B` | fails (no spec) |
| `google/gemma-4-E2B-it`, `google/gemma-4-E4B-it` | start with an `audio` warning (declared, no audio processor); image served |
| `meta-models/Muse-Glimmer-30B` | fails (no spec for `muse_glimmer`) |
| `Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B`, `Qwen/Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct`, `Qwen/Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct` | start |
| `TinyLlama/TinyLlama-1.1B-Chat-v1.0`, `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B` (text-only) | start |

E2E on one GB200 GPU per case, with `VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1` and a release `vllm-rs` from this change (run before the rebase onto `92b9817e02`, which adapts to the new `mm_processor_kwargs` argument and the HY4-VL spec without changing these inputs, and before the third commit, which only changes the Gemma 4 start below):

| Start | Result |
|---|---|
| `vllm serve HuggingFaceTB/SmolVLM-256M-Instruct` | the Rust frontend exits with the no-spec message below |
| same + `--language-model-only` | healthy; a text chat completion returns 200 |
| same + `--limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image": 0, "video": 0, "audio": 0}'` | healthy; a text chat completion returns 200 |
| `vllm serve google/gemma-4-E2B-it` | before the third commit the Rust frontend exited; it now starts with the `audio` warning below (model load only, not re-run end to end) |
| same + `--limit-mm-per-prompt '{"audio": 0}'` | healthy; a chat completion with a red 64x64 PNG answers "Red" |

Rust frontend CI lane steps that start multimodal models: `pytest -v -s entrypoints/serve/instrumentator/test_metrics.py -k "not run_batch and not test_metrics_exist and not multimodal"` 6 passed; `pytest -v -s v1/core/prefix_cache/test_hybrid_prefix_cache_hit_rate.py` (`Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B`) 2 passed.

## Details

- **Why fail instead of warn.** Python's `ModelConfig._supports_multimodal_inputs` also warns and runs text-only, but there the model itself has no processor. Here the engine supports the media and only the frontend drops it, so the request-time error ("`image` input is not supported by this model") misleads. A model the frontend serves partly only warns, since failing would take away the modalities that work (Gemma 4 images). This is a Rust-frontend decision, not a Python parity gap; it also lets a future `auto` frontend selection learn from a Rust startup check that a model needs the Python frontend.
- **Where the check lives.** `MultimodalModelInfo::from_paths` / `from_loaded` (`vllm-chat`), which resolve the spec and the per-modality lanes at model load, so the check sees exactly what Rust can serve. "Has a multimodal config" is the set of preprocessor config files that same function reads: `preprocessor_config.json`, `video_preprocessor_config.json`, and the `image_processor` / `video_processor` / `feature_extractor` sections of `processor_config.json`. A spec's declared modalities come from `ModelProcessorSpec::modality_limits`, which each spec derives from the checkpoint config (Qwen3-VL declares video only with `video_token_id`). `from_loaded` now takes the resolved spec instead of looking it up in each lane resolver, and records the declared modalities it cannot serve so the per-request error can name the Rust frontend. The new errors are typed variants of `vllm_chat::Error`.
- **Messages:**

  Launch error (no spec, or no declared modality resolves):

  ```
  the Rust frontend cannot serve multimodal input for model `HuggingFaceTB/SmolVLM-256M-Instruct` (model_type `idefics3`); pass --language-model-only to serve it as a text-only model, or set VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=0 to use the Python frontend
  ```

  Launch warning and per-request error for a partly served model (`google/gemma-4-E2B-it`):

  ```
  the Rust frontend does not support `audio` input for this model, and requests carrying it will be rejected; pass --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"audio": 0}' to disable it, or set VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=0 to use the Python frontend
  ```

  ```
  `audio` input is not supported by the Rust frontend for this model; set VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=0 to serve it with the Python frontend, or pass --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"audio": 0}' to disable it
  ```
- **Behavior change for forced-Rust deployments.** Users who run a model the Rust frontend cannot serve any media of with `VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1` as text today must add `--language-model-only`.
- **Rust frontend CI lane** (second commit, `.buildkite/test_areas/rust_frontend.yaml`). The only multimodal models the lane starts are `HuggingFaceTB/SmolVLM-256M-Instruct` (the `multimodal` parametrization of `entrypoints/serve/instrumentator/test_metrics.py`) and `Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B` (`v1/core/prefix_cache/test_hybrid_prefix_cache_hit_rate.py`, which resolves the `qwen3_vl` spec and starts). `Qwen/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-FP8` and `meta-llama/Llama-4-Scout-17B-16E-Instruct` appear in the lane's test files but are deselected there. The lane's SmolVLM cases (`test_metrics_counts`, `test_abort_metrics_reset`) only send text and its image case `test_metrics_exist` is already excluded, so the step deselects `multimodal`; the Python lanes keep the SmolVLM coverage. `pytest --collect-only` with the new `-k` selects the 6 text cases (was 12).
- **Test harnesses.** The `vllm-chat` roundtrip tests render and parse text through real checkpoints, one of which (`muse_glimmer`) now refuses to load with media, so `load_roundtrip_backends` passes `language_model_only: true`; likewise the renderer-selection fixtures in `backend::hf::tests`.

**Not a duplicate.** Searched open PRs (`rust multimodal language-model-only`, `rust frontend multimodal spec`, `rust multimodal unsupported launch`, `spec is not registered`). vllm-project/vllm#68808 (Nemotron VL and Omni specs) and vllm-project/vllm#58649 (Gemma 4 image spec) add model specs; they are compatible with this check (a model whose spec lands starts instead of failing) and do not change the launch behavior for models without one.

**AI assistance.** This change was developed with AI assistance (Claude Code). The human submitter reviewed every changed line and the validation results.

commits.pr_title: [HiSparse] Share the host pool per node under multi-node TP
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

HiSparse's shared host pool (#56629) only applied to single-node TP. With TP spanning nodes (e.g. TP8 over two 4-GPU nodes), every rank fell back to a private pinned pool, so `host_pool_gib: 150` pinned 600 GiB per node even though MLA host KV is replicated and every rank gets the same host block IDs. Reported in #68725 (this PR doesn't address that issue's eviction bug).

Now each node gets one shared pool:

- `use_shared_hisparse_host_pool` no longer requires `nnodes_within_dp == 1`.
- `get_hisparse_host_leader_rank` returns the lowest TP rank on the node (`tp_rank // local_world_size * local_world_size`). That rank creates the node's `SharedOffloadRegion`, which is named per leader, and is the node's only host writer (prefill DMA and host-block CoW).
- Pre-faulting is sharded across the node's ranks (`populate_shard=(tp_rank % local_world_size, local_world_size)`), so every node's region is fully populated.
- Readers take the writer's IPC events from their own node's leader: an `all_gather_object` over the TP CPU group replaces `broadcast_object(src=0)`, because IPC handles can't cross nodes.
- The TP-wide barrier stays. It also works across nodes, since each node's creator unlinks its file only after every rank has mapped its own.

Single-node behaviour is unchanged: the leader is TP rank 0 and the populate shard is `(tp_rank, tp_size)`. Host block count and stride are derived from config alone, so they're identical on every rank and node.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/test_shared_offload_region.py -k "hisparse or populate or barrier or mp_"
pytest tests/v1/worker/test_utils.py tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_planning.py -k hisparse
```

- New `test_mp_hisparse_host_pool_is_shared_per_node` runs the real `allocate_hisparse_host_pools` in 4 processes, as 1 node × 4 ranks and as 2 nodes × 2 ranks. It checks one inode per node, that each node's ranks together pre-fault its whole region, that each node's leader writes are visible only to that node's ranks, and that SIGKILL leaks no `/dev/shm` files. It fails if the region name drops the per-node suffix or the populate shard uses global TP ranks.
- Unit tests cover leader selection, picking IPC events from the node leader, the node-local populate shard, and that the shared-pool gate now accepts multi-node TP.

## Test Result

**Unit tests** (Linux, CPU only): 76 passed. The 8 failures (`test_hisparse_pool_must_fit_max_model_len`, `test_hisparse_host_copy_waits_for_writes_on_writer_only[True-*-0]`, `test_hisparse_cache_handles_join_index_groups_during_construction`) need a GPU and fail identically on `main` there.

**GPU, GLM-5.3-NVFP4, B200, `--nnodes 2`**

Two setups:
- **Split single node:** 1 node × 4 B200, TP4, run as two `--nnodes 2` halves of 2 GPUs each. This is still the multi-node path (`local_world_size=2`, leaders `tp0`/`tp2`). PR (`0b26befda2`) vs `main` (`a51047055c`).
- **True 2-node:** 2 nodes × 4 B200, TP8, for the per-node memory check (an earlier `main`, same region logic).

The GPU KV cache is capped at 4096 blocks so that requests are host-backed and decode gathers hot-buffer misses from the host pool.

Settings applied identically to `main` and the PR, all for pre-existing issues:
- `VLLM_ALLREDUCE_USE_SYMM_MEM=0`, `VLLM_ALLREDUCE_USE_FLASHINFER=0`, `--disable-custom-all-reduce`, `fuse_allreduce_rms=false`. Without them, symm-mem, custom-AR MNNVL, and FlashInfer AR setup hang or retry when TP spans nodes without multi-node NVLink.
- A `sitecustomize` providing `os.memfd_create` via libc. The test machines use python-build-standalone CPython, which lacks it, and the multi-segment `SharedOffloadRegion` needs it (single-node TP on `main` hits this too).

```bash
vllm serve <GLM-5.3-NVFP4> -tp 4 --nnodes 2 --node-rank {0|1} --master-addr <head> [--headless] \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 64 --max-model-len 8192 --max-num-seqs 16 --num-gpu-blocks-override 4096 \
  --attention-config '{"hisparse_config":{"device_buffer_size":2048}}' \
  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"HiSparseConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"host_pool_gib":32}}'
vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --random-input-len 4096 --random-output-len 512 \
  --num-prompts 96 --max-concurrency 16 --ignore-eos --seed 42
python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8123 --num-shots 20 --num-questions 500 --max-concurrency 64
```

| | `main` | PR |
|---|---|---|
| Host pools, split node | 4 private pinned pools | 2 regions (`..._tp0`, `..._tp2`), Shmem 67 GB (2 × 34 GB, fully populated) |
| Host pools, 2-node TP8 | one private 32 GiB pool per rank (4 per node) | one 32 GiB region per node (`..._tp0`, `..._tp4`), Shmem +34 GB per node |
| Host writer ranks | all 4 | `tp0`, `tp2` (`tp1`, `tp3` only read) |
| Hot-buffer misses per rank (bench + GSM8K) | 303M (all ranks) | 309M (all ranks, incl. readers `tp1`, `tp3`) |
| `hisparse_host_to_device_bytes_total`, GSM8K | 2.19 TB | 2.24 TB |
| GSM8K 20-shot, 500 q | 0.882 | 0.892 |
| Output tok/s | 228.2 | 227.9 |
| Mean TPOT (ms) | 12.43 | 12.46 |
| Mean TTFT (ms) | 27101 | 27130 |

In each half, the leader logs `Created mmap file ..._tp{leader}.mmap`, its peer logs `Opened existing mmap file`, and the leader then unlinks it. The reader ranks gather the same number of misses from their node's pool as the writers, and accuracy and latency match `main`, so readers see the node leader's writes and waiting on its event costs nothing measurable.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Fix collect_env.py crash on non-Linux platforms
commits.pr_body:
Replaces #45162, which was closed when the source fork was detached.

## Purpose

`get_env_info()` calls `get_pkg_version()` on non-Linux platforms, where its Linux-only assertion aborts the environment report.

Return `None` instead so the report can complete. Linux lookup behavior is unchanged.

## Test Plan

Tested from the source checkout on macOS 15.6 arm64 with Python 3.12.13 and PyTorch 2.14.1:

```bash
python -m vllm.collect_env
```

## Test Result

- Before: `AssertionError` in `get_pkg_version()`, no environment report.
- After: exits 0 and prints the environment report.

Local Linux package-lookup fixtures also produced the same results and command sequences before and after the fix. Windows/Linux were not tested natively.

## Overview

Move `:nvidia: (H200) EC Filesystem Tiering` (`ec-filesystem-tiering`, added in #63294) from the whole-node `h200` queue to a 35GB MIG slice (`h200_35gb`), where most single-GPU H200 steps already run. The step uses one GPU (`num_devices: 1`), so it does not need a whole 8-GPU node.

## Claims

- The step keeps its PR-selection rules and stays non-optional; it now runs on `h200_35gb` instead of `h200`.
- No change to what it runs.

## Validation

- `pre-commit run --files .buildkite/test_areas/misc.yaml` passes.
- Scoped build of only this step on this head (f7dd887): https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/105455 passed on a 35GB MIG slice, `2 passed in 477.03s` (`single` and `concurrent`), no retries. 
- Full `/ci run` after rebasing (9a33ca8): https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/105461 passed; normal PR selection picked the step on the 35GB MIG queue, `2 passed in 285.19s`, no retries. The job stays well under its 45-minute timeout.

## Details

The test starts two vLLM servers one after the other, each serving `Qwen/Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct` in BF16 with `--max-model-len 4096`, `--enforce-eager` and `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.8`. That fits in a 35GB slice (about 17 GB of weights); an 18GB slice would not.

The whole-node `h200` queue is shared with other pipelines, so a single-GPU step there can wait a long time for a free node and hold the PR build open.

Builds created before this merges keep their already-queued `h200` copy of the step; a rebuild or new push picks up the MIG queue.

Not a duplicate: no open PR touches this step (`pr-dupes search EC Filesystem Tiering`).

commits.pr_title: [Core] Remove dead pcp_world_size plumbing from KV cache managers
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Remove dead `pcp_world_size` plumbing from the KV cache core layer (`KVCacheManager`, `KVCacheCoordinator`, `SingleTypeKVCacheManager`, `Scheduler`, and callers), since KV cache block ownership is now determined solely by `dcp_world_size` after MRV2 virtual-batch PCP (#46570).

- **Why this is not duplicating an existing PR**: Searched open PRs on `vllm-project/vllm` for `pcp_world_size`, `kv_cache_coordinator pcp`, and `KVCacheManager pcp`; no open PR addresses this cleanup.
- **Related PRs**: #28718 (originally introduced `pcp_world_size` in KV cache managers), #46570 (decoupled PCP from KV cache block sizing), #56723 (replicated draft with DCP/PCP).

## Claims

- Removes unused `pcp_world_size` parameters, attributes, docstrings, and unreachable PCP assertions across `KVCacheManager`, `KVCacheCoordinator` (all subclasses + factory), `SingleTypeKVCacheManager` (all subclasses), `Scheduler`, `SimpleCPUOffloadScheduler`, and `UMBPStoreConnectorScheduler` (`7 files changed, 5 insertions(+), 59 deletions(-)`).
- Removes the unused `AttentionSpec` import in `vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_coordinator.py` and the unused `Scheduler.pcp_world_size` attribute.
- No functional or behavioral change: `Scheduler` and `SimpleCPUOffloadScheduler` already hardcoded `pcp_world_size=1`, and real PCP compatibility checks live in `PCPManager.validate_config` and `check_attention_cp_compatibility`.


## Details

### Why `pcp_world_size` was originally needed

In the original MRV1 PCP implementation (#28718), KV cache storage was sharded across the combined `dcp_world_size * pcp_world_size` ranks, so each logical block spanned `spec.block_size * dcp_world_size * pcp_world_size` tokens. As a result, `Scheduler` had to pass `pcp_world_size` into `KVCacheManager` → `KVCacheCoordinator` → `SingleTypeKVCacheManager` and `find_longest_cache_hit` so that:
1. `SingleTypeKVCacheManager.block_size`, `UnitaryKVCacheCoordinator.block_size`, and `FullAttentionManager.find_longest_cache_hit` could scale the logical block size by `dcp_world_size * pcp_world_size`.
2. Non-full-attention managers (`SlidingWindowManager`, `ChunkedLocalAttentionManager`, `MambaManager`, and `HybridKVCacheCoordinator`) could guard against `pcp_world_size > 1`.

### Why `pcp_world_size` is no longer needed

Under MRV2 virtual-batch PCP (#46570), **prefill compute sharding (PCP)** and **KV cache storage sharding (DCP)** are cleanly decoupled:

1. **KV cache layout and block sizing depend solely on `dcp_world_size`**:
   - When `PCP > 1, DCP = 1`, KV cache is replicated across PCP ranks (`ParallelConfig.pcp_shard_decode_requests` documents this invariant directly), so logical `block_size` is unscaled.
   - When KV cache is sharded across PCP (or `TP × PCP`) ranks, `ParallelConfig` enforces `dcp in (1, pcp, tp * pcp)` (`vllm/config/parallel.py`), so KV sharding is fully represented by `dcp_world_size`.
   - Accordingly, #46570 already removed all `block_size *= pcp_world_size` scaling from `SingleTypeKVCacheManager`, `UnitaryKVCacheCoordinator`, and `FullAttentionManager.find_longest_cache_hit`, and changed `Scheduler` to hardcode `pcp_world_size=1`.
   - On the planning and worker sides, `vllm/v1/kv_cache_interface.py`, `vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_planning.py`, and `BlockTables` (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py`, initialized with `cp_size=self.dcp_size, cp_rank=self.dcp_rank`) never consult `prefill_context_parallel_size`.
2. **All remaining references in `vllm/v1/core/` were dead plumbing**:
   - `Scheduler.pcp_world_size` was unused anywhere in the repo, and both `Scheduler` and `SimpleCPUOffloadScheduler` hardcoded `pcp_world_size=1`.
   - `SingleTypeKVCacheManager.pcp_world_size` was never used in any allocation, caching, or lookup computation—only forwarded into `assert pcp_world_size == 1` checks that were unreachable from `Scheduler`.
   - The only runtime caller passing a non-1 value was `UMBPStoreConnectorScheduler._lookup_coordinator`, which uses `get_kv_cache_coordinator` purely for prefix lookup and does not depend on PCP behavior.
3. **PCP compatibility validation belongs in startup/worker validation (and already lives there)**:
   - `PCPManager.validate_config` (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/pcp_manager.py`) validates MLA / speculator / PCP+DCP constraints.
   - `check_attention_cp_compatibility` (`vllm/v1/worker/cp_utils.py`) validates `backend.supports_pcp()` per attention layer.
